stem: Altostrat Media must move large volumes of newly recorded audio and video from legacy on-premises ingestion systems into Cloud Storage every day. Reliability is a top priority, the transfers must not cross the public internet, and the team wants predictable throughput for sustained bulk traffic. Which connectivity design best fits?

choices.text: A Dedicated Interconnect topology with redundant connections in two metropolitan areas, so that ingestion keeps running if one path or one metro is lost
Direct Peering with Google at an edge location, so that the ingestion servers reach the Cloud Storage buckets over private IP addresses
One HA VPN gateway pair over the public internet, with Cloud Router sharing routes, so that encryption is the only protection the traffic needs
A single Dedicated Interconnect connection in one metro with a Classic VPN tunnel as the backup path, so that the redundant path stays cheap to run

stem: A retail group has about forty product teams, each in its own project. A central network team must own subnets, routes and firewall rules, while product teams only deploy workloads into approved subnets. All workloads must talk to each other over internal IP addresses. Which design fits?

choices.text: One VPC network per project joined by Cloud VPN tunnels, with the network team reviewing every team's tunnel settings
A single project for all teams, with Identity and Access Management roles limited to the instances each team creates
Shared VPC with a host project owned by the network team and each product project attached as a service project
VPC Network Peering between every pair of product-team VPC networks, with each team writing its own firewall rules

stem: A software vendor hosts a managed analytics service in its own VPC network on Google Cloud. Hundreds of customers, each with its own VPC network, must consume it privately. Many customer networks use overlapping private ranges, and the vendor does not want customers to reach anything except the service. Which TWO design points fit this requirement? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Create a VPC Network Peering connection from the vendor network to every customer network
Publish the service behind an internal load balancer through a Private Service Connect service attachment
Merge the vendor and all customer subnets into one Shared VPC network owned by the vendor
Have each customer create a Private Service Connect endpoint with an internal IP address from its own VPC network
Give the service an external IP address and let each customer allowlist the vendor's firewall rules

stem: A manufacturer has four plants, each with its own site network connected to Google Cloud by Cloud Interconnect or HA VPN, and a VPC network holds shared services. The plants also need to exchange data with each other, and the team wants to use the Google network for this instead of buying a separate private WAN. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Cloud NAT gateways in each region so that plants translate their addresses and reach each other through the internet
A full mesh of VPC Network Peering connections between per-plant VPC networks, with each plant's site network behind its own VPC network
Network Connectivity Center as a hub, with each plant's hybrid connection attached as a spoke and site-to-site data transfer enabled
A Private Service Connect endpoint in every plant, so that each site publishes its whole network as a service

stem: Altostrat Media stores a huge, growing archive of audio and video in Cloud Storage. Some episodes become popular years later, so access is unpredictable, and the team does not want to maintain lifecycle rules that guess which objects are cold. Storage cost must fall without lowering availability. Which design fits best?

choices.text: A bucket in the Archive storage class, so that every object gets the lowest storage price regardless of how it is read
A bucket with Autoclass enabled, which moves each object between storage classes automatically according to how it is accessed
A Filestore instance mounted on the editing servers, so that frequently read files stay on high-performance disks
Lifecycle rules that move every object to Coldline after 30 days, so that cost falls on a fixed and predictable schedule

stem: A financial reporting service stores regulatory documents in Cloud Storage. Compliance requires that data stay in two specific European regions, the application must keep working without any path changes if one region fails, and the recovery point objective for new writes should be short and predictable. Which bucket design fits?

choices.text: A dual-region bucket in the two required regions, with turbo replication turned on
A multi-region bucket in the EU location, because it spreads objects across several European regions
A regional bucket in one required region, with a nightly copy job to a regional bucket in the second region
A regional bucket plus Object Versioning, so that earlier versions of objects can be restored after a failure

stem: A growing software-as-a-service team runs its customer data on SQL Server on premises and wants to move to Google Cloud with the lowest administration effort. The application uses T-SQL features and needs a high-availability setup with automatic failover inside one region, but does not need global writes or horizontal scaling beyond a single primary. Which database choice fits?

choices.text: SQL Server on Compute Engine VMs in a managed instance group, so that the team controls the operating system
Bigtable, because it scales writes by adding nodes and removes the need for a relational schema
Spanner, because it replicates across regions and removes the need to think about the database engine
Cloud SQL for SQL Server with a high availability configuration, which fails over to a standby in another zone

stem: A global ticketing platform stores orders in a relational schema and must accept writes from users in North America, Europe and Asia at the same time. Orders need strong consistency and ACID transactions across regions, and the platform must keep serving during a regional outage without manual failover. Which database fits?

choices.text: Spanner in a multi-region configuration, which provides strongly consistent transactions across regions with synchronous replication
Bigtable with multi-cluster replication, which keeps clusters in several regions eventually consistent with one another
Firestore in Datastore mode with one regional location, which scales automatically for key-based reads and writes
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL with cross-region read replicas, which serve reads close to users while one primary takes the writes

stem: An automotive supplier collects sensor readings from millions of connected devices, each sending a small record every second. The team needs single-digit-millisecond lookups by device and time range, sustained write rates in the hundreds of thousands per second and no complex joins. Which storage service fits?

choices.text: Memorystore for Redis, holding all readings in memory with a persistence snapshot
Cloud SQL for MySQL, with one table per device and an index on the timestamp column, on a large primary instance with read replicas
Bigtable, with a row key that starts with the device identifier and ends with a time component
Cloud Storage Standard, with one object per reading and a prefix per device, listed by prefix and time range

stem: A team lifts and shifts a legacy application to Compute Engine. The application expects a shared POSIX file system mounted by several VMs, uses file locking and cannot be changed. The first design stored the files in a Cloud Storage bucket, but the application fails on file semantics. What is the best storage design?

choices.text: A single Persistent Disk attached read-write to every VM in the instance group
Local SSD on each VM, with a scheduled rsync job copying files between the machines
A Cloud Storage bucket mounted through Cloud Storage FUSE, with the application writing files in place
A Filestore instance, exported as an NFS share and mounted by all application VMs

stem: Altostrat Media needs a small piece of code that runs whenever a new video lands in a Cloud Storage bucket. It extracts metadata and writes it to the warehouse, runs for a few seconds per file, and the team wants no servers or clusters to operate and no cost while idle. Which compute choice fits?

choices.text: Compute Engine VMs in a managed instance group that scale on CPU utilization
Cloud Run functions triggered by the bucket event
A Cloud Run job scheduled hourly by Cloud Scheduler, regardless of when files arrive
A GKE Standard cluster with a Deployment that polls the bucket every minute

stem: A platform team runs about thirty microservices on Kubernetes. Several require privileged DaemonSets for a node-level security agent and a specific kernel setting on nodes, and the team already has Kubernetes operations skills. Another team asks which GKE mode fits these workloads. What is the best answer?

choices.text: Cloud Run functions, because each microservice can be wrapped as a function and the nodes disappear
GKE Autopilot, because it is the recommended mode and permits privileged node-level components too
GKE Standard, because it gives control over node configuration and allows the privileged node-level components
Cloud Run, because it runs any container and supports privileged DaemonSets on its own infrastructure

stem: KnightMotives builds a simulation environment to test autonomous-driving software. Thousands of independent simulation runs, each lasting minutes, are queued in batches overnight. A failed run can simply be restarted, and the team wants the lowest compute cost. Which compute choice fits?

choices.text: Sole-tenant nodes reserved for the simulation project, so that other customers never share the hardware
A single very large VM running all simulations in sequence, so that only one machine ever needs patching
Standard on-demand VMs sized for peak load and kept running around the clock, so that no run is ever interrupted
Spot VMs in a managed instance group or a batch service, with jobs written to restart when a VM is preempted

stem: A team moves a legacy application to Compute Engine. The vendor says it needs 8 vCPUs and 40 GB of memory; none of the predefined machine types matches closely, and the memory-heavy sizing would waste money on unused vCPUs. The workload will run for several years at steady load. Which TWO actions reduce cost best? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Select the largest predefined memory-optimized machine type to leave headroom for future growth
Buy resource-based or flexible committed use discounts for the steady, predictable usage
Place the VM in a dual-region location to reduce its hourly price through regional pricing
Run the application only on Spot VMs, since a long-running legacy application restarts cleanly
Create a VM with a custom machine type that has the exact vCPU and memory ratio the vendor needs

stem: EHR Healthcare must ingest claims and clinical updates from new provider partners. Volumes spike unpredictably, events arrive continuously, records must be cleaned and enriched within seconds, and the results land in BigQuery for analytics. The team wants no clusters to size. Which processing design fits?

choices.text: Pub/Sub to receive events, a streaming Dataflow pipeline to transform them, and BigQuery as the destination
Compute Engine VMs running a self-written consumer, with a fixed number of instances behind a load balancer
A Managed Service for Apache Spark cluster that is created manually each morning and sized for the expected peak
A nightly batch export of all partner files to Cloud Storage, followed by a scheduled BigQuery load job

stem: Cymbal Retail wants shoppers to find products by typing natural-language questions on its website and app, with results ranked using the catalog and shopper behavior. The team prefers a managed service tuned to retail over building its own search stack. Which product choice fits?

choices.text: AI Commerce Search in Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience, the managed retail search service
Memorystore for Redis holding a copy of the catalog, queried with exact-match key lookups
Cloud Storage with a static index file for every product category, which the browser downloads and filters locally
BigQuery with a LIKE query over product titles, exposed through a custom web service

stem: A bank wants to extract fields from thousands of scanned loan applications with fixed layouts (names, addresses, amounts) into structured records, with confidence scores so that low-confidence documents can be routed to a human reviewer in the bank's own workflow. Which AI product choice fits best?

choices.text: Cloud Translation, because it can read text in scanned images and return it in a chosen language
Document AI, with a processor for the document type and a review queue fed by low confidence scores
Training a custom image classification model on Compute Engine GPUs to label the scans by document type
Prompting a general chat model by hand for every scanned page, and copying answers into a spreadsheet

stem: A research lab wants to pretrain a large custom model on its own data, with a distributed job running across hundreds of accelerators for weeks and needing high-bandwidth, low-latency networking and fast storage. Which infrastructure choice fits?

choices.text: A fleet of general-purpose E2 VMs in a managed instance group, trained with the CPU only
Calling a hosted Gemini model through the Gemini API with a long prompt that includes the training data
AI Hypercomputer, using GPU or TPU clusters with high-performance networking and parallel storage
Cloud Run services with GPUs attached, scaled out as one instance per accelerator

stem: Altostrat Media wants a 24/7 support chat assistant that answers viewer questions using only the company's own program guides and policies, cites the source of each answer, and does not invent shows that do not exist. Which TWO design choices fit this goal? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Train a new foundation model from scratch on the guides using AI Hypercomputer GPU clusters
Turn off all grounding and rely on a higher sampling temperature to make answers more varied and engaging
Fine-tune a model once on a snapshot of the guides and expect it to know every later schedule change
Ground the model's answers in the company's documents using a managed retrieval-augmented generation setup, such as Agent Search over the guides
Build the assistant with Conversational Agents or an agent on the Agent Platform, using a foundation model such as Gemini

stem: EHR Healthcare runs containerized applications on several Kubernetes clusters in Google Cloud and on premises, managed by different teams with different configurations. Past outages came from misconfiguration. The company wants consistent policy, configuration and visibility across all clusters. Which design fits?

choices.text: Replace Kubernetes with Compute Engine VMs and manage them with startup scripts that each team edits locally
Register the clusters in a fleet with GKE Enterprise, and apply shared configuration and policy through fleet features
Move all workloads into one very large cluster in a single region, so that there is only one configuration to maintain
Keep each cluster independent and document the standard settings in a shared wiki page for the teams to follow

stem: A company runs batch analytics on private Compute Engine VMs and on-premises servers. Security rules say none of these machines may have external IP addresses, yet all of them must call Google APIs such as Cloud Storage and BigQuery without traffic crossing the public internet. The on-premises servers connect to the VPC network through Cloud Interconnect. Which design fits?

choices.text: Enable Private Google Access on the VM subnets, and point on-premises hosts at the Private Google Access virtual IPs over the Interconnect
Assign external IP addresses to all VMs and restrict egress with firewall rules, because Google APIs need a public address
Create a Classic VPN tunnel from every on-premises server straight to the Cloud Storage service endpoint
Create a separate VPC Network Peering connection between the on-premises network and Google's API network

stem: An architect is turning a retailer's workshop notes into a requirements document. Which TWO of the following statements are non-functional requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Customers must be able to save several delivery addresses in their account profile
The warehouse team must be able to export the daily picking list as a spreadsheet file
Support agents must be able to refund a single line item from an order that they are viewing on screen
The order service must keep accepting orders when one zone of its region is unavailable
Checkout pages must respond within a set time at the 95th percentile during promotions

stem: A parcel-tracking company runs a customer portal, a driver dispatch system and an internal HR portal. The board asks for a business continuity plan that is affordable. A workshop shows that a dispatch outage stops revenue within minutes, the customer portal can tolerate a few hours of downtime, and the HR portal can be unavailable for days. What should the architect do first when shaping the continuity design?

choices.text: Defer all continuity design until after migration, then apply the cheapest backup schedule to every workload to keep the budget simple
Ask each application team to choose its own continuity design independently, then merge the results without comparing them to business impact
Run a business impact analysis, then give each system its own recovery time and recovery point targets
Deploy every system with the strongest multi-region active-active design, so the same continuity target applies to all workloads without exception

stem: EHR Healthcare promised hospitals at least 99.9% availability. In the draft design, a customer-facing request passes in series through the web tier, an API tier and a database, and each of the three has its own availability objective of 99.9%. What should the architect tell management about the promise?

choices.text: The combined availability of the chain is lower than 99.9%, so tighten the dependency targets or add redundancy
The promise is met, because each component individually reaches the 99.9% target that was stated
The promise is irrelevant, because availability objectives apply only to the database and not to the whole request path
The promise is met, because adding more serial components makes the chain more reliable than any single one

stem: A SaaS company will run about the same number of vCPUs and amount of memory in one region on Compute Engine for the next three years. Another team's workloads, on a different machine series and in other regions, change every few months. The finance lead wants the biggest discount that does not risk paying for unused commitments. Which plan fits?

choices.text: Buy no commitments and rely on on-demand rates for both teams, since commitments cannot be matched to a changing set of workloads
Buy three-year resource commitments for the variable team's current machine series in each region it uses
Buy resource-based commitments for the steady footprint and a modest flexible commitment for the variable part
Buy one large spend-based commitment sized to the peak of both teams, because a spend commitment is always cheaper than a resource commitment

stem: A company moving to Google Cloud has three product teams that share one billing account. Executives want each team to see its own spend, receive warnings before a monthly limit is exceeded, and be able to trigger automated responses to a runaway cost. Which TWO actions support this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Move every team into one project so that only a single budget needs to be maintained
Disable billing on the shared account whenever any team approaches its target, so that all spending stops at once
Ask each team to read the monthly invoice and report increases manually, which avoids any tooling
Apply consistent labels or separate projects per team so billing data can be broken down by team and exported for analysis
Create per-team Cloud Billing budgets with alert thresholds and use the notifications to trigger automated responses

stem: Cymbal Retail exchanges orders with suppliers through nightly SFTP file drops and batch ETL, and a failure in one step silently delays everything after it. The business wants new gen AI catalog enrichment and order tracking to react as events happen, and wants to add consumers later without changing producers. Which integration pattern best meets this?

choices.text: Load all data into one shared relational database and let each application read the tables it needs at any time
Publish business events to Pub/Sub topics and let each consumer subscribe independently
Have each producing application call every consuming application's API synchronously and wait for each reply
Keep the nightly files but have every consumer poll the SFTP server each minute to cut the delay between the steps

stem: A logistics firm runs an on-premises PostgreSQL database for shipment tracking. Analysts need the data in BigQuery within seconds of each change, the source must keep serving the live application, and the team wants no servers of its own to run for the replication. Which approach should the architect choose?

choices.text: Run a self-managed replication tool on Compute Engine virtual machines that the team itself patches, monitors and scales
Rewrite the application so that it writes every record to BigQuery and the database at the same time
Schedule a nightly full export of every table to files and load them to BigQuery with a batch job
Use Datastream change data capture into BigQuery over private VPN or Interconnect connectivity

stem: A broadcaster must copy hundreds of terabytes of archived video from its on-premises NAS to Cloud Storage over an existing 1 Gbps link that also carries daily business traffic. Past ad hoc copies using scripts stalled and were restarted by hand. Leadership wants a reliable, scheduled, verifiable transfer that can be throttled during working hours. Which solution fits?

choices.text: Storage Transfer Service with on-premises agents, scheduling, retries and bandwidth limits
A single long-running copy script on one workstation that is restarted by an operator after every interruption
Streaming each file through Pub/Sub messages so the broker handles retry and bandwidth sharing for the copy
Mounting the Cloud Storage bucket on each employee's laptop so that editors can drag and drop the video files straight into it

stem: KnightMotives wants a CRM and dealer toolset covering sales, service and inventory. The company's in-house teams are stretched by fragmented legacy code and technical debt, dealers have no budget for new equipment, and the business wants value within months. Which disposition best balances time to value and risk?

choices.text: Modify the legacy dealer application in place by adding new modules to its existing code base and servers
Deprecate the dealer tooling without replacement, because dealers can use spreadsheets until the new data platform is complete
Buy a browser-based dealer-management and CRM product and integrate it through APIs
Build a custom CRM from scratch with the in-house teams so that every feature matches current internal processes exactly

stem: EHR Healthcare is moving customer-facing systems to Google Cloud and promised hospitals at least 99.9% availability. Management also wants proof that the move is paying off after one year. Which set of key performance indicators best fits these goals?

choices.text: Count of alert emails sent per month and the number of dashboards created in the monitoring tool
Monthly availability of customer-facing services against the 99.9% target, plus unit cost per practice versus the colocation baseline
Total number of virtual machines created, number of projects in the organization and number of engineers who completed training courses each quarter
Total count of services migrated, regardless of their availability, cost or the number of incidents after migration

stem: In a requirements workshop, a media start-up's product owner asks for "the lowest possible latency worldwide, the highest availability, and the lowest possible cost". The architect knows these goals pull against each other. What is the best next step?

choices.text: Choose the highest availability design with global multi-region replication, since cost can be reduced later without redesigning it
Quantify each goal with the business as a latency percentile, an availability target and a cost ceiling, then rank them
Record all three goals as written and let the engineering team decide the trade-offs during implementation without further review
Choose the lowest cost design, because availability and latency can be improved after launch simply by adding more servers to it

stem: A manufacturer compares keeping its data center against moving a steady ERP-reporting workload to Google Cloud. The CFO asks for a fair business case. Which analysis is most defensible?

choices.text: Compare only the list price of equivalent virtual machines to the purchase price of servers, and ignore all other items
Treat the on-premises hardware as free since it is already purchased, and compare only the cloud bill with zero
Compare the monthly cloud bill to server depreciation alone, ignoring facilities, staffing and migration effort
Compare the full multi-year cost of both options, including refresh, facility, staff, cloud run costs and migration effort

stem: KnightMotives plans to replace its mainframe supply-chain and ERP system gradually, because a big-bang cutover could halt plants and dealers. Which approach to the future improvement of this system reduces risk the most?

choices.text: Copy the mainframe to virtual machines unchanged and declare the modernization finished, since the hardware is then gone
Let each plant choose and build its own replacement on its own timeline, so no central design is needed
Put an API layer in front of the legacy system, move one capability at a time behind it and retire legacy parts as traffic moves
Freeze legacy changes for years while a full replacement is built, then switch all plants over in one weekend

stem: Cymbal Retail's pilot for gen AI product descriptions produced good drafts, and the merchandising lead wants to extend it to the whole catalog next month. Wrong descriptions would reach customers directly, and compliance reviewers have not seen the process. What should the architect recommend for the next phase?

choices.text: Expand in stages with human review before catalog updates, measuring accuracy and rejection rates at each step
Stop the program until models never produce an error, since any human review proves that the approach is unsuitable
Publish every generated description for the entire catalog automatically and fix errors when customers complain
Replace the pilot with a hand-written description process for every product, to avoid any new risk from automation

stem: An architect reviews a platform that has run on Google Cloud for two years. The team wants a standing way to find savings in idle and oversized resources and to feed them into the improvement backlog. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: Wait for a cost spike on the invoice, then ask engineers to guess which resources are the cause
Ignore recommendations and rely on a yearly purchase of a larger commitment to lower the unit price of everything
Review Active Assist recommendations regularly, weigh saving against risk and schedule accepted changes in the backlog
Apply every recommendation automatically on the day it appears, in all environments, with no owner review or testing first

stem: A platform team learns that the Container Registry service it uses for build images has been shut down and that Cloud Deployment Manager has reached end of support. The roadmap has no time for platform work. What does this show about planning future improvements, and what is the best response?

choices.text: Treat each retirement as an emergency, pause all feature work and migrate everything at once in a single release
Track deprecation notices and migrate to the supported replacement, such as Artifact Registry, on a schedule
Pin all pipelines to the retired tool and write private scripts to emulate it, so that nothing needs to change
Retirements can be ignored because running workloads continue indefinitely without any change to them at all

stem: An architect is asked to propose a new analytics capability for next year's roadmap. A promising Google Cloud feature is labelled Preview in the documentation. The capability would support a regulated production workload with contractual availability targets. What is the best way to treat the feature in the roadmap?

choices.text: Exclude every Preview feature from all future planning, including proofs of concept and vendor conversations
Build the production design around it and plan to replace it quickly if it is retired, so no testing is required
Adopt it for production immediately, because every Google Cloud feature has the same support commitments as a generally available one
Evaluate it in a non-production proof of concept and commit production use only after general availability

stem: A company has a list of eight improvement ideas for its Google Cloud platform: reduce toil in deployments, pay down database schema debt, add a new language to the mobile app, refactor a rarely used admin tool, and so on. The platform team can deliver only three this quarter. Which TWO practices produce the best prioritisation? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Weigh dependencies, so that enabling work that unblocks several other improvements is sequenced early
Postpone all technical debt until a calm period, since debt does not accumulate interest like financial debt
Always start with the cheapest items, regardless of what they achieve, to show progress in the number of tickets closed
Fund the items whose owners argue most loudly, since seniority indicates the importance of each item
Score items on business value, risk reduced and effort, favouring those that address measured incidents and delays

stem: After launching a new subscription service, a team's backlog fills with reliability work and new features, and nobody agrees which to do. The service has an availability objective, and the monthly data show that the service has consumed most of its error budget by mid-month. How should the architect use this data to plan improvements?

choices.text: Shift the next iteration toward reliability work until the error budget is no longer being consumed too fast
Continue shipping features at full pace, since the error budget is only a reporting number that has no bearing on planning
Remove the objective entirely, because it creates conflict between feature work and reliability work
Raise the availability objective to a stricter value so that the remaining budget looks larger

stem: EHR Healthcare wants insights and predictions from provider data, and many new providers will send data in different formats over the next two years. The architects are proposing a roadmap. Which sequence is the most sensible?

choices.text: Keep each provider's data in its own separate database indefinitely and run reports by hand on request
Postpone all analytics until every provider has migrated to one common data format, and offer no insights before then
Train predictive models on whatever each provider sends, then design ingestion and quality processes afterwards
Centralise ingestion and governed storage with quality checks, then build analytics, then add predictive models

stem: A company's roadmap for the next three years lists features that must be portable between cloud providers if its strategy changes. A team suggests building the order database on a proprietary managed service because its performance is the best. How should the architect treat portability in this decision?

choices.text: Require identical architectures to run unchanged on two providers at all times, so that any workload can move at any time
Ignore portability completely, because switching providers is never a realistic possibility for any company
Weigh lock-in cost against benefit, using portable interfaces only where exit risk is material and managed services elsewhere
Avoid every managed service and run self-managed open source software everywhere to eliminate any dependency

stem: A news site's traffic is highly spiky: a few viral stories cause bursts that last minutes, and most of the day it runs at a fraction of its peak. It runs on a fixed fleet of virtual machines sized for the peak, and the CFO asks the architect for the next-year improvement with the greatest cost effect and the least operational work. Which proposal is best?

choices.text: Keep the fleet unchanged and add a second identical fleet in another region so that every peak is shared between the two
Move the stateless front end to a serverless or autoscaled platform and keep a small latency-critical baseline
Reduce the fleet to the average load size permanently and accept slow pages during viral peaks
Buy a three-year commitment on the entire fixed fleet at peak size, to get the discount on all of the capacity

stem: Twelve months after a platform migration, leadership asks how to decide what to improve next. Which TWO sources give the architect the most reliable evidence for the next roadmap? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The number of new Google Cloud products announced in the last year, since adopting more of them shows platform maturity
The original project plan, since it already defined all improvements that will ever be required
The preferences of the most senior stakeholder, as expressed in the next steering meeting
A post-implementation review that compares the KPIs set before the project with the values measured now
Operational telemetry such as incidents, latency, error rates and cost reports from the running platform, trended over time

stem: A company adopts a cloud-first policy. A year later, a regional hospital group's imaging system, which depends on a certified on-premises device and a 10 ms link to the scanners, is proposed for migration. How should the architect apply the policy?

choices.text: Move it immediately, because any exception to a cloud-first policy weakens it and creates precedent for others
Exempt every workload that has ever had a special requirement, so that most of the estate stays on-premises
Treat cloud-first as a default: keep this workload on-premises with hybrid connectivity and revisit later
Rewrite the policy so no workload may remain on-premises and press the vendor to certify the device in the cloud

stem: A manufacturing company is closing two data centers and moving its workloads to Google Cloud. The finance director welcomes the end of large hardware purchases but worries that monthly bills will now vary and could surprise the business. As the architect, which advice best addresses both the benefit and the concern?

choices.text: Explain that cloud costs are fixed once a project is created, so the monthly bill always matches the first estimate and no monitoring or tagging is needed
Explain that spending moves from capital purchases to usage-based operating costs, and add budgets with alerts, labels and committed use discounts for the steady baseline
Recommend buying the maximum expected capacity up front for three years on every service, so the bill stays predictable but the company keeps capital-style commitments
Recommend moving only the cheapest workloads at first and delaying any cost reporting until the migration is complete and the usage has stabilized

stem: A company's cloud bill is growing, and 40 teams share a few projects. Finance cannot tell which product or team causes the growth, and engineers suspect many oversized and idle VMs. Which TWO actions give finance and engineering the data to attribute and reduce the spend? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Apply consistent resource labels, one project per team or product, and export detailed billing data to BigQuery for reporting by team
Ask every team to estimate its own monthly usage in a spreadsheet and send it to finance at the end of each quarter
Move all workloads into one large project so that a single total appears on the invoice
Buy committed use discounts for the full current spend first, and look at which resources are idle or oversized only after the commitment is in place
Review the idle and rightsizing recommendations that Google Cloud generates from observed usage and resize or remove the flagged resources

stem: EHR Healthcare's customer-facing systems must reach at least 99.9% availability, and the company is about to choose disaster recovery designs for dozens of services. The architect wants the business to agree on what each design must achieve before any design is priced. What should be done first?

choices.text: Run a business impact analysis that ranks each service by the harm of an outage and assigns recovery time and recovery point objectives per service tier
Choose multi-region active-active deployments for all services, since that gives the highest availability and the business can accept the cost
Ask each engineering team to describe its current backup schedule and treat the existing schedule as the recovery requirement
Copy the disaster recovery approach of the largest competitor, because that is a proven design for electronic health record software

stem: A retailer wrote a business continuity plan that says "restore the order system in another region within one hour". During a real regional outage the restore took six hours, because nobody had practised the steps and a configuration secret existed only in the failed region. How should the plan have been validated?

choices.text: Increase the size of the backup storage, because a larger backup shortens the time needed to restore the system
Replace the plan with a statement that the order system uses a managed service, so no recovery steps, owners or runbooks need to be documented any more
Review the written plan once a year in a meeting, since the document already states the one-hour objective clearly
Run scheduled failover exercises to the second region, record the actual recovery time and fix every gap found

stem: EHR Healthcare onboards insurers one after another and wants to show that the cloud move helps these customers succeed, not only that systems are running. Which set of measures best shows customer success?

choices.text: Number of container clusters deployed and the percentage of workloads already migrated from the colocation facility
The count of alerts sent by the monitoring system per month and the number of tickets closed by the operations team
Time to onboard a new insurer, availability and latency of customer-facing APIs against objectives, and satisfaction or ticket trends
Server CPU utilization, the number of virtual machines running and total monthly cloud spend, reported every week to the engineering director and finance

stem: Altostrat Media runs transcoding of its video library as batch jobs that can restart from a checkpoint and have flexible deadlines, while its recommendation service must always be on. Reliability and cost are both top priorities. Which compute purchasing approach is the best fit?

choices.text: Run both workloads on standard on-demand VMs only, because mixing purchase options makes cost reporting too complex
Cover the always-on recommendation baseline with committed use discounts, and run the restartable transcoding jobs on Spot VMs
Reserve capacity for the full peak of transcoding all year, so jobs never wait and the recommendation service can share the same pool
Run both the transcoding jobs and the recommendation service on Spot VMs, because Spot capacity is the cheapest option available

stem: A software company is moving its customer billing system to Google Cloud over a weekend cutover. The business cannot accept a failed migration that leaves invoices unprocessed. Which plan best protects business continuity during the migration?

choices.text: Shut down the old system before the cutover starts so that no data can change while the data is copied
Keep the old system in sync, rehearse the cutover, agree a go/no-go checkpoint with a tested rollback, and retire the old system after a stable period
Migrate a copy of the data to the cloud first and delete the original data right away to save cost
Switch all traffic at once during the weekend, rely on the support team to fix any problems on Monday morning, and shut the old system down immediately after the switch

stem: A bank offers a payments API to partner fintechs. Each partner has a contract with a monthly request allowance. Separately, the operations team wants to protect the backend from sudden bursts of traffic from any single caller. Which TWO Apigee policies match these two needs? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The Quota policy, which counts requests per app or developer over a period such as a month and enforces the contractual allowance
The SpikeArrest policy, configured with a monthly count so that it tracks each partner's contract
The ResponseCache policy, which stores successful backend answers so the backend does not receive any requests
The Quota policy, set to a very short period, as the only mechanism both for contracts and for burst protection
The SpikeArrest policy, which smooths the rate of requests that reach the backend to protect it from sudden surges

stem: An insurer exposes claims APIs to partners. A new contract states that API traffic must be processed in the insurer's own facilities, where it already runs a Kubernetes platform, but the insurer still wants Google-hosted API management, analytics and a developer portal. Which Apigee approach fits best?

choices.text: A custom gateway on virtual machines in the insurer's data center, maintained by the insurer's team without Apigee components
Apigee with a fully Google-hosted runtime, because the data stays inside Google Cloud, which is the same as the insurer's own facilities
Apigee for the partner developer portal only, while API traffic is sent unmanaged directly to the backend
Apigee hybrid, with the runtime plane installed on the insurer's own Kubernetes platform and the management plane hosted by Google

stem: A public transport authority publishes a timetable API. The data changes every ten minutes, yet thousands of apps request the same routes, and the backend database is struggling at rush hour. The team wants to relieve the backend without changing its code and accepts answers that are a few minutes old. Which Apigee capability fits?

choices.text: A VerifyAPIKey policy, since checking keys removes the load that comes from valid callers
A Quota policy that limits each app to one request per day so that traffic stays low
A ResponseCache policy that serves stored responses for identical requests between data refreshes
A SpikeArrest policy set to reject every second request, so that the number of backend calls is halved

stem: Cymbal Retail wants its suppliers to submit product data through an interface instead of SFTP file drops. The retailer needs to know which supplier calls what and how often, give each supplier its own credentials and request allowance, and add new API versions without breaking existing suppliers. Which platform choice fits these needs best?

choices.text: A public Cloud Run service on its default URL with IAM disabled and request logs reviewed by hand each week
One shared API key for all suppliers placed in the onboarding email, with limits applied inside the backend code
Continued SFTP uploads with a nightly script that moves files into Cloud Storage, a spreadsheet of supplier activity, and version numbers agreed by email
Apigee API management, with API products, per-app credentials, quotas, analytics and versioned proxies in front of the backend

stem: A hospital group runs a self-managed MySQL database on premises with an order-entry application. It will move the database to Cloud SQL for MySQL, and the application can tolerate only a few minutes of downtime. Which approach should the architect advise?

choices.text: Use Datastream to stream changes into BigQuery and point the order-entry application at BigQuery
Stop the application, export the database to a dump file, copy it by hand and import it, then restart the application on the new database
Use Database Migration Service for an initial load and continuous replication, then promote the destination during a short cutover
Rewrite the application to write to both databases through custom code, and compare the results after a month

stem: A manufacturer wants to move an Oracle database that holds many stored procedures to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL to cut licensing cost. The architect is asked what Database Migration Service does for this heterogeneous move and what the team must still do. Which statement is accurate?

choices.text: Database Migration Service converts the schema and code in a conversion workspace and migrates the data, but the team must fix unconverted objects and test the application
Database Migration Service guarantees that converted applications behave identically, so functional testing is no longer needed after cutover
Database Migration Service migrates only the table data; every schema object and stored procedure must be rewritten by hand before any job can start
Database Migration Service copies the Oracle data files as they are into PostgreSQL, so schema and procedures run without conversion or review

stem: KnightMotives has several hundred terabytes of test-drive sensor recordings at a rural proving ground whose network link is slow and shared with plant operations. The company wants the data in Cloud Storage within weeks for analytics. Which method fits best?

choices.text: A single script on a laptop that copies the files over the existing link and is left running until it finishes
Transfer Appliance, filled on site and shipped to Google, which uploads the data to Cloud Storage
Storage Transfer Service agents saturating the shared link around the clock, which would disrupt plant operations
Streaming the recordings into Pub/Sub topics from every test vehicle in real time

stem: A media company keeps 200 TiB of archive in Amazon S3 and wants a full copy in Cloud Storage, followed by recurring syncs of new objects. It has good bandwidth, and the data team prefers not to maintain custom code. Which approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use Storage Transfer Service from S3 to Cloud Storage on a recurring schedule, with parallel transfers, retries and integrity validation
Export the S3 objects to a Cloud SQL database and then export them again to Cloud Storage in batches
Ship the S3 data on a Transfer Appliance, because appliances are the only supported way to move more than 100 TiB of data into Cloud Storage
Write a custom program that lists the S3 bucket, downloads each object to a VM and uploads it, and run it on a schedule

stem: Altostrat Media must move VM-based legacy content-ingestion servers from its on-premises environment to Compute Engine. The servers run licensed software that the vendor will not let the team change. The business wants the least modification and a short outage per server. Which tool and approach fit best?

choices.text: Export each VM to a file, email the file to the cloud team and recreate the settings by hand
Use Migrate to Virtual Machines to move each server unchanged to a Compute Engine instance, with its operating system and software
Rewrite each ingestion server as a Cloud Run function and migrate the data separately
Use Database Migration Service to move the servers, since it copies all data and settings from any source system to Google Cloud

stem: Cymbal Retail keeps order data in MySQL and SQL Server on premises. Analysts need these changes in BigQuery within seconds of occurring, without adding load or custom code to the transactional systems. Which service should the architect recommend?

choices.text: Transfer Appliance, which captures changes from the databases and returns them as a BigQuery table
A nightly export job that dumps the tables to files, which analysts load into BigQuery the next morning
Datastream, a serverless change data capture service that replicates database changes into BigQuery with minimal latency
Storage Transfer Service, which copies database tables as objects from on-premises storage on an hourly schedule

stem: Altostrat Media wants its engineering teams to deliver containerized services through dev, staging and production with consistent, centrally managed promotion and approval rules. What should the architect advise?

choices.text: Give all teams permissions to push images directly into the production cluster, relying on code review for control
Let each team write its own deployment script, because delivery differences between teams are best left to the teams
Standardize on one CI tool for all teams, and have engineers apply the Kubernetes manifests to each environment by hand after the build
Define a Cloud Deploy pipeline with ordered targets and approvals, and have each team's build process create releases from its container images

stem: A team releases a new version of a Cloud Run service. It wants to expose the version to a small share of real traffic, observe errors, and be able to return to the previous version immediately. Which TWO actions support this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Deploy the new revision and send it all traffic, then ask users to report problems by email
Delete the previous revision as soon as the new one starts, to avoid confusion about which version serves traffic
Deploy the new revision without sending it all traffic, then route a small percentage of requests to it and increase the share when metrics look healthy
Create a second Cloud Run project with the new version and ask users to switch to its URL
Keep the previous revision available and, if errors rise, route all traffic back to it

stem: A team deploys a new application version that changes a database column from one format to another. It uses a blue/green release for safety, but after switching traffic, the green version works while rolling back to blue fails because blue cannot read the new column format. What should the architect advise for future releases?

choices.text: Never roll back; always fix forward, because rollback strategies are not reliable when a database exists
Make schema changes in backward-compatible steps so both versions work, and drop the old format after the rollback window
Run each version on its own separate database so the schema is independent, and merge the two databases by script each night
Change the schema first to the new format, and keep the old application version offline until the new version has proven itself in production

stem: A development lead plans the automated tests for a new microservice. Unit tests finish in seconds, integration tests take minutes, and a full load test takes two hours. How should the architect advise placing them in the pipeline?

choices.text: Unit tests on every commit, integration tests on merge in an ephemeral environment, and the load test before release in a production-like environment
Skip the unit and integration tests when the load test passes, to save pipeline time
Run all tests only manually before production, so the pipeline remains as fast as possible for developers
Run only the two-hour load test on every commit, because it is the most realistic test and makes faster tests redundant for the team

stem: A company has migrated a 5 TB PostgreSQL database to Cloud SQL and wants to decide on cutover. Which TWO validation activities best show that the migrated system is ready? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Delete the source tables as soon as the migration job reports its first copy of the data, to prevent users from writing to the source
Check only that the migration job's status shows "running", since that confirms data is correct
Run the migration job a second time to the same destination so duplicates confirm the data exists
Replay a representative set of production queries and application test cases against the destination and compare results and latency with the objectives
Compare row counts and checksums or sample records between source and destination for the critical tables

stem: EHR Healthcare suffered past outages in which email alerts went unnoticed. The operations lead wants to shorten the time from alert to understanding the cause across a multi-tier service. Which Gemini Cloud Assist capability helps most directly?

choices.text: A replacement of Cloud Monitoring alerting policies, which makes it unnecessary to define any alerts
An automatic fix that applies production configuration changes without review whenever a problem is detected in any monitored service
Proactive alert investigations, where an alert triggers Gemini Cloud Assist to cluster related alerts and draft a root-cause analysis
Natural-language drafting of status-page and customer notices, so that outage announcements are written and published faster by the team

stem: A platform team wants to use Gemini Cloud Assist to speed up designing a new three-tier application and writing the Terraform for it. The security lead is concerned about unreviewed AI output reaching production. What should the architect advise?

choices.text: Apply the generated Terraform directly to production, because Gemini Cloud Assist already knows the project's organization policies and standards
Avoid Gemini Cloud Assist, because AI-generated infrastructure code can never be made safe for production
Use Gemini Cloud Assist output only for the application code and write all infrastructure from memory without any templates
Use Gemini Cloud Assist to draft the design and Terraform, then run it through code review, policy checks and the CI/CD pipeline

stem: A software company runs development and test environments on Compute Engine VMs that developers use only during working hours, yet the environments run around the clock and are among the largest cost lines. Which approach optimizes resources most appropriately without hurting developers?

choices.text: Delete the environments and let developers test directly on the production systems, which already run all day and carry real customer data
Stop the non-production VMs outside working hours and recreate disposable environments from infrastructure as code
Buy three-year committed use discounts sized to the current always-on usage of these environments
Move the environments to larger machine types, so that tests finish faster and the VMs can be stopped sooner

stem: A healthcare analytics company stores patient-derived datasets in BigQuery and Cloud Storage. A recent penetration test showed that an engineer with valid IAM permissions, or an attacker holding that engineer's stolen credentials, could copy a dataset to a bucket in an unrelated external project and read it there. The architect must close this path without removing the engineer's legitimate roles. Which control addresses it?

choices.text: Place the projects in a VPC Service Controls service perimeter so that calls to BigQuery and Cloud Storage cannot move data to resources outside it
Remove the engineer's data roles and re-grant them at the dataset and bucket level only, so that no principal holds a project-wide data role
Add an IAM Conditions expression to every data role that limits access to the corporate IP address range of the engineer's office network
Require customer-managed encryption keys on both services so that data copied to an outside project stays unreadable without the key

stem: A bank wants to wrap its 40 production analytics projects in a VPC Service Controls perimeter. These projects serve nightly reports, a partner data feed and several internal tools, and the team cannot list every legitimate caller. Enforcing immediately could break business-critical jobs. What is the best rollout?

choices.text: Enforce the perimeter on a single project first, keep the other 39 outside, and add the rest one at a time after each project has run without incident
Create the perimeter with only the partner feed's service account as a member, so the partner flow is covered first and all other projects stay unaffected
Create the perimeter in dry run mode, review the audit log entries for would-be violations, add ingress and egress rules for legitimate flows, then enforce it
Enforce the perimeter and include every service in the restricted services list, then ask teams to open support tickets for each blocked job and add exceptions afterwards

stem: A security architect is designing VPC Service Controls for a company that keeps regulated data in two separate perimeters, one owned by research and one by finance, and sometimes needs controlled sharing between them. Which TWO statements describe the correct design? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Ingress and egress rules let the two perimeters exchange only specified identities, services and methods, so the sharing path is explicit and narrow
Perimeters replace Cloud NGFW rules, so VPC firewall rules and firewall policies can be removed from the protected projects once the perimeter is enforced
Any metadata about a protected resource, such as bucket names, is always blocked from callers outside the perimeter without exceptions
Putting a project in a perimeter makes IAM unnecessary for it, because the perimeter now decides every access decision for the protected services
VPC Service Controls complements IAM, so a request needs both a matching IAM permission and to satisfy the perimeter boundary rules to succeed

stem: A group of 300 projects across several folders must use customer-managed encryption keys for Compute Engine disks, BigQuery datasets and Cloud Storage buckets. The security team wants keys to be created on demand in a central key project, with key administration separated from the developers, and developers and Terraform pipelines must not need Cloud KMS admin rights. Which design fits?

choices.text: Keep Google-managed encryption for all services and rely on a single shared key in the central project for the few datasets that auditors ask about
Use Cloud KMS Autokey with dedicated-project key storage: each folder's Autokey config names the central key project, and keys appear as developers create resources
Create one Cloud KMS key in the central project and share it with all 300 projects so key administration stays in one place
Pre-create a key ring and key for every service in every project, and give each team Cloud KMS Admin on its own keys so it can attach them

stem: KnightMotives Automotive has suffered past data breaches and must meet EU data protection rules for its new data management platform. Its security team wants the guarantee that no new Compute Engine disk, BigQuery dataset or Cloud Storage bucket in the organization can be created without a customer-managed key, and that the keys can only come from the central key project. Which TWO organization policy settings meet this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Set gcp.restrictCmekCryptoKeyProjects to deny the central key project, so that Cloud KMS keys become unusable from any project of the organization
Grant the Organization Policy Administrator role to every project owner so each team can enforce encryption on its own projects
Enable Data Access audit logs on Cloud KMS, which blocks resource creation whenever no key is specified
Set the constraint gcp.restrictNonCmekServices on the organization, listing the services that must always use CMEK for newly created resources
Set the constraint gcp.restrictCmekCryptoKeyProjects on the organization, allowing only the central key project as source of CMEK keys

stem: A European insurer's regulator requires that encryption keys for its core claims data stay outside the cloud provider's infrastructure under the insurer's own custody, and that the insurer can make the data unreadable at any moment by withdrawing key access. The workloads run on Google Cloud services that support CMEK. Which key design meets this?

choices.text: Cloud KMS software keys in a key ring in the same region as the data, with automatic rotation, a separate administrator group and disabled key export
Cloud External Key Manager (Cloud EKM) keys held in a partner's external key manager, with Google's access granted by the insurer and revocable
Cloud HSM keys in the same region, whose key material lives in hardware security modules that Google operates for the insurer
Customer-supplied encryption keys sent in each API request, which makes every client application responsible for key transport

stem: Two firms want to pool sensitive customer records for joint fraud analysis on Compute Engine VMs. Each firm already encrypts data at rest and in transit, but a firm's risk team worries that an administrator of the hypervisor or a compromised host could read the data while it is being processed in memory. Which design addresses that specific risk?

choices.text: Require TLS 1.3 between the two firms' systems and restrict connections with firewall rules to the partner's IP ranges
Enable VPC Flow Logs on the subnets so that any unexpected host access to the VMs is recorded for review
Add a second layer of customer-managed encryption keys to the persistent disks that hold the records
Move the analysis to Confidential VMs, which keep data encrypted in memory and isolate it from the host and hypervisor

stem: Cymbal Retail is moving its web catalog services and batch integrations to GKE and Cloud Run. Today the MySQL and Redis passwords sit in container environment files and in config repositories, and nobody can say who has read them. The security team wants central storage, per-service access, an access trail, and the ability to rotate credentials without rebuilding images. Which design fits?

choices.text: Store the credentials in Secret Manager, grant each workload's service account access to only its own secrets, and read the current version at runtime
Move the passwords into a private Cloud Storage bucket with uniform bucket-level access, mount the bucket into each container as a file system, and rely on object versioning for rotation history
Encrypt the environment files with a Cloud KMS key and commit the encrypted files, so that only holders of decrypt rights can read them
Keep the passwords in Kubernetes Secrets in each cluster, and give platform engineers the cluster-admin role to rotate them

stem: A company encrypts its data warehouse with a key in a dedicated key project. The auditor asks for a design in which no single group can both manage keys and use them to decrypt data. Which TWO assignments achieve this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Grant the security team's key administrators Cloud KMS CryptoKey Encrypter/Decrypter on all keys so they can verify that rotation works
Grant the data engineers Cloud KMS Admin on the key ring so they can rotate and disable keys as they ingest data
Grant the security team's key administrators Cloud KMS Admin on the key project, a role that manages keys but cannot encrypt or decrypt with them
Grant every data engineer Owner on the key project so any incident can be resolved without waiting for the security team
Grant the BigQuery service agent the Cloud KMS CryptoKey Encrypter/Decrypter role on only the key it protects

stem: EHR Healthcare must be able to answer, for each medical office tenant, who read patient files stored in Cloud Storage and when. Today only the default audit logs exist. The logs must be tamper-resistant and viewable by the security team but not by the engineers who operate the platform. Which design meets this?

choices.text: Enable Data Access audit logs for Cloud Storage on the folder, and route them with an aggregated sink to a locked log bucket in a separate security project
Enable Data Access audit logs only on the platform projects, and store them in the log bucket of each project, so that each engineering team can review its own access
Rely on Admin Activity audit logs, which already record every read of a patient file, and route them to the engineers' project for convenience
Enable VPC Flow Logs on the clusters, which record the object names and users for each file read through the Cloud Storage API

stem: A company blocks creation of service account keys across the organization with an organization policy, but one legacy folder runs a vendor product that cannot yet use keyless authentication. The exception must be limited to that folder, with every other folder staying blocked. What is the right design?

choices.text: Remove the policy from the organization and set it separately on each of the other folders, so the legacy folder simply has none
Enforce the policy at the organization and create an IAM deny policy on the legacy folder that allows key creation for the vendor's account
Keep the policy enforced everywhere and grant the vendor's service account the Organization Policy Administrator role so that it can create its own keys
Set the policy at the organization to enforce the restriction, and override it with a policy on the legacy folder that does not enforce it

stem: A platform team grants project owners broad rights to run their own environments. The CISO now wants a rule that nobody, including project owners and organization administrators, can delete the central audit log buckets or disable log sinks, except a small break-glass group. Allow policies on thousands of projects are managed by many teams. Which control is the most robust?

choices.text: Remove the logging roles from every project owner by editing each project's allow policy in turn, and have a script re-check all of the policies each month
Create a custom role named logging-readonly and ask teams to use it instead of the basic roles
Add an IAM deny policy at the organization that denies those logging permissions to everyone, with the break-glass group as an exception
Set an organization policy constraint that forbids owners from signing in to the Google Cloud console outside business hours

stem: EHR Healthcare is moving several Kubernetes environments to Google Cloud and wants a central rule that SSH and RDP from the internet are denied on every VM network in the organization, with no project administrator able to override it. Application teams still need to define their own allow rules for service ports. Which design applies?

choices.text: Place a Cloud NAT gateway in front of each network so that inbound SSH and RDP can never reach a VM from the internet
Create a hierarchical firewall policy at the organization with a deny rule for SSH and RDP from the internet and goto_next for all other traffic
Create a global network firewall policy in one shared project and attach it to the networks of that project, then ask the other teams to copy the same rules
Create VPC firewall rules in each project that deny the SSH and RDP ports, and publish the standard rule in a runbook for teams to copy

stem: A company hosts an internal HR web application on Compute Engine behind an external Application Load Balancer. Employees and a few contractors reach it from home, and the team wants to remove the VPN and avoid depending on network location. Access must depend on the signed-in identity and group membership, with the application receiving the identity from the platform. Which design fits?

choices.text: Open the load balancer to the internet with a Cloud Armor rule that allows only the employees' home IP addresses
Add a login page to the application itself and store employee passwords in the application database
Keep the application private, and require every user to connect through a corporate VPN with a shared pre-shared key per department, as before
Enable Identity-Aware Proxy on the load balancer's backend, grant the allowed groups the IAP-secured Web App User role, and verify its signed header

stem: A manufacturer's dealers need to use the company's SaaS CRM and an internal inventory web app from their own laptops and phones, because the company cannot buy equipment for them. The security team wants access only from devices that meet baseline posture checks, data loss prevention in the browser (for example blocking downloads of customer lists to unmanaged storage), and threat protection. Which solution fits?

choices.text: Managed Chromebooks shipped to every dealer, enrolled and locked down by the company
A site-to-site VPN to each dealership, giving every dealer office a route into the corporate network
Chrome Enterprise Premium, with context-aware access based on device posture plus browser data protection and threat controls
An organization policy constraint that restricts which external SaaS domains and web applications can be reached from the company's Google Cloud projects

stem: A software company deploys to Google Cloud from a SaaS CI/CD platform outside Google Cloud. Today the pipeline uses an exported service account key stored as a CI variable, and the key was exposed in a build log last quarter. The security team wants to remove long-lived credentials and make sure only the production pipeline of one repository can deploy to production. What is the best design?

choices.text: Create a workload identity pool and provider for the CI platform's OIDC tokens, map the repository claim, and let only that repository impersonate the deployer account
Create a new service account key per pipeline run, delete it after the run, keep it in the CI platform's secret store, and restrict key creation to the pipeline's identity
Rotate the exported key monthly and mask it in build logs, keeping the same service account for all repositories
Give the CI platform's user account the Owner role on the production project, so no service account is needed at all

stem: A holding company is setting up its Google Cloud organization for three business units, each with production and non-production workloads. Security wants centrally enforced guardrails, business units that manage their own projects, and access that can be reviewed without reading thousands of project policies. Which hierarchy and IAM design is best?

choices.text: One folder for the whole company, with the Owner role granted to the business units' leads on that folder
One folder per business unit with production and non-production subfolders, guardrail policies and group-based IAM set at the folders
A flat set of projects directly under the organization, with a unique allow policy per project, users granted roles individually by email, and reviews done project by project
A separate Google Cloud organization for each business unit, so that each unit has full independence and a separate super admin

stem: A cloud architect found that hundreds of principals hold the legacy Editor basic role on production projects, granted years ago during migration. The security team wants to reduce these permissions without breaking jobs. Which TWO actions fit the process? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Use Cloud Audit Logs Admin Activity entries as the permission list, and copy each principal's logged API calls into a custom role
Delete every Editor binding on Friday evening and wait for users to report what stopped working over the weekend
Use Policy Simulator to test the proposed allow policy change against recent access activity before applying it
Replace each Editor binding with Owner so that all permissions remain available and no job fails during the change
Use role recommendations (IAM recommender) to see which permissions each principal actually used and to suggest narrower roles for the excess grants

stem: Database administrators currently hold the Owner role on production projects permanently, even though they need elevated rights only a few times per month for maintenance. The security team wants elevated access to be temporary, justified, approved and fully auditable. What should the architect implement?

choices.text: Create a shared admin account and rotate its password after every maintenance window
Use Privileged Access Manager (PAM) entitlements, so administrators request time-limited elevation with justification, approval and audit trail
Keep standing Owner grants but require two-step verification for the administrators' accounts
Grant the administrators a broad predefined admin role through an IAM Condition that applies only on weekends and only to requests from the corporate network

stem: A company has about 400 projects created by different teams. The security director wants a single view of misconfigurations such as publicly exposed buckets, vulnerable workloads, and threats, across the whole organization, with findings prioritised and routed to the security team. Which service should be the core of the design?

choices.text: Security Command Center activated at the organization level, aggregating findings from detection services across projects
Cloud Monitoring dashboards with an alerting policy per project, maintained by each team for its own resources
Cloud Asset Inventory exports to BigQuery, queried manually by an analyst each week for public resources
An organization policy that blocks all public exposure, with no reporting because violations are no longer possible

stem: A retailer wants its marketing analysts to run behavioural analysis in BigQuery on customer support transcripts that contain names, email addresses and phone numbers. Analysts must be able to join records that belong to the same customer across tables, and a small privacy team must be able to restore the original email address when a legal request requires it. Which de-identification approach fits?

choices.text: Delete the personal data columns and keep a copy in a bucket that only the privacy team can open
Mask each value with asterisks using a character masking transformation, which keeps the format of the field but cannot be reversed later
Replace every value with a fixed placeholder such as REDACTED, so that no analyst can derive anything about a customer from the data
Use Sensitive Data Protection with a cryptographic transformation, such as deterministic or format-preserving encryption using a KMS-wrapped key

stem: Altostrat Media is launching a 24/7 natural-language support chat that uses an LLM, with customers also able to paste text. The security review requires that adversarial prompts trying to override system instructions are blocked, that harmful content is filtered in both directions, and that customers' personal data is not returned in model responses. Which design addresses all three?

choices.text: Add a regular-expression check in the chat web page that blocks suspicious words before submitting the prompt
Restrict the chat to authenticated users with Identity-Aware Proxy, which then prevents any harmful content from being typed or returned
Put a Model Armor template in front of the model to screen prompts and responses for prompt injection, harmful content and sensitive data
Rely on the model's built-in training to refuse unsafe prompts, since it is a managed foundation model

stem: Altostrat Media manages CI/CD for containers that run on GKE clusters in Google Cloud and on-premises. After a supply chain scare, the architect must ensure that only images built by the approved Cloud Build pipeline and that passed vulnerability checks are deployed to production clusters. Which design enforces this?

choices.text: A written policy telling developers to deploy only images from the team's Artifact Registry repository, checked in quarterly audits
A VPC firewall rule on the cluster nodes that allows egress only to the Artifact Registry service address
An IAM role that lets only the CI service account push images, with nothing restricting where the cluster pulls images from
Binary Authorization on the production clusters, with a policy requiring attestations from the build and vulnerability-check attestors

stem: Cymbal Retail keeps product cost, supplier margin and customer contact columns in the same BigQuery tables that merchandisers, the marketing team and a gen AI catalog enrichment pipeline query. Merchandisers must see everything except margin; marketing must see contact data but not margin; the pipeline must see neither. The tables should stay one copy. What is the best design?

choices.text: Classify the sensitive columns with policy tags and grant the fine-grained reader role on each tag only to the groups allowed to see that data
Create three copies of each table with different columns and keep them in sync with scheduled queries
Put each team in its own project and rely on project-level IAM, so that dataset roles decide who can read which column of the shared tables
Encrypt the sensitive columns in the application and distribute the keys by email to the groups that need them

stem: A financial company runs regulated workloads on Google Cloud. Its policy states that Google support or engineering staff may access its content only after a named company administrator has explicitly approved each request, and the company must keep a record of every approval. Which Google Cloud capability supports this?

choices.text: A VPC Service Controls perimeter around the project, which stops all Google staff from reaching its resources at the network layer and logs the attempts
Access Approval, which requires an authorized customer administrator to approve each Google personnel request before access
An IAM deny policy at the organization that denies the project's data permissions to every principal except the company's own administrators
Access Transparency logs alone, which list the Google personnel actions after the fact

stem: A company's security review found that its three Cloud Identity super admin accounts are used for daily administration and are protected by passwords only. Which TWO changes follow Google's recommended practice? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Use the super admin account as the identity for service accounts so that automation never loses access
Share one super admin account among all the administrators so that its credentials and recovery details are managed in a single place
Grant the Organization Administrator role to a private admin group for daily work and keep super admin accounts out of that group
Disable two-step verification on super admin accounts to avoid being locked out during an incident
Give each super admin a separate account used only for super admin tasks, and enforce two-step verification with physical security keys

stem: A multinational with 30,000 employees uses Microsoft Entra ID as its identity provider and wants staff to sign in to the Google Cloud console and tools with their existing corporate identities. The security team does not want to create or synchronise a Google identity for every person, and wants access to be granted from IdP group claims. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Workforce Identity Federation, which maps IdP identities and attributes into a workforce pool that IAM can use in policies
Directory-wide service account keys issued to each employee, distributed through the HR onboarding process
Workload Identity Federation with a pool for each employee, so that every person has a separate federated pool principal
Consumer Google accounts created by employees with their corporate email addresses and added to groups manually
