stem: A company does not know where personal data lives across hundreds of BigQuery datasets and Cloud Storage buckets that teams created over several years. Before it can apply access controls, the architect needs to find out which tables and buckets contain sensitive data and how risky each is. Which approach is the most efficient?

choices.text: Run a one-time inspection job on a random 1 percent sample of every bucket and table, and treat unflagged ones as clean and ready for sharing
Use Sensitive Data Protection discovery to profile data across the organization or folders, and use the findings to drive policy tags and access decisions
Ask each team to review its datasets and report back with a spreadsheet of sensitive columns and buckets
Move all data into a single new project so that the security team can browse it manually

stem: EHR Healthcare is moving a customer-facing records portal to Google Cloud. The stateless web tier must keep serving users if one zone of the region fails, and the MySQL database behind it must fail over without anyone restoring a backup. The company accepts a few minutes of database interruption during a zonal failure but wants to avoid the cost of running in several regions. Which design fits?

choices.text: Two regional managed instance groups in different regions behind a load balancer, plus a Spanner multi-region instance for every table in the application database
A zonal managed instance group with a fast snapshot schedule, plus a Cloud SQL for MySQL instance with a single zone and a nightly export to a Cloud Storage bucket
A single large Compute Engine VM in one zone that relies on live migration for host maintenance, plus a self-managed MySQL server on a persistent disk of that VM
A regional managed instance group behind a load balancer, plus Cloud SQL for MySQL in a high-availability configuration with a standby in a second zone

stem: A logistics company has classified its order-management system as needing a recovery time objective of 4 hours and a recovery point objective of 15 minutes if the primary region is lost. The business will not fund a full second production environment. The database is MySQL. Which disaster recovery pattern fits best?

choices.text: No separate pattern: a single regional deployment, since zone redundancy covers a regional outage
Cold pattern, with nightly backups restored into an empty second region only after a disaster has been declared by the incident team
Hot pattern, with two fully scaled production stacks serving live production traffic in two regions at all times
Warm standby: a cross-region database replica plus a scaled-down copy of the stack, scaled up on failover

stem: A company runs a Cloud SQL for MySQL instance with high availability enabled and a cross-region read replica. A script run by an administrator drops a production table by mistake, and ransomware protection is also a board concern for the backup copies. The team learns that the standby and the replica both already show the table as gone. Which TWO measures protect against this kind of logical damage? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Enable automated backups with point-in-time recovery so the database can be restored to a moment just before the faulty statement
Raise the instance to a larger machine type, so that a failover to the standby completes faster after such an error
Add a second cross-region read replica so that one more copy of the data exists in another location
Switch the instance to a multi-region Cloud Storage bucket for its data files, so objects are stored in several locations
Use Backup and DR with a backup vault, whose write-once-read-many immutability keeps protected backups from being altered or deleted

stem: Cymbal Retail expects holiday traffic several times higher than normal for a few days. Its web tier stores each shopper's cart in the memory of the VM that served the first request, so the load balancer is configured with session affinity and the team can only grow capacity by buying larger VMs. Which change best prepares the tier for the peak?

choices.text: Move to a spot-VM fleet of identical size, because the lower price per VM allows the team to over-provision all year
Keep the design, order the largest available machine type, and let each VM hold more carts in its memory
Move cart state to Memorystore for Redis, make the web VMs stateless, and run them in an autoscaled managed instance group
Move the web tier into a single zone on high-CPU VMs, so all requests reach machines in one network location

stem: Altostrat Media serves podcasts and documentaries to viewers on several continents. Media files are in Cloud Storage and the origin application is in one region. Viewers far from the region see slow start times for popular episodes, while the origin is lightly loaded. Which change most directly reduces latency for these viewers?

choices.text: Increase the replication of the media archive to a dual-region location and keep serving viewers from the same two regions
Put a global external Application Load Balancer in front, with Cloud CDN enabled so popular objects are cached close to the viewers
Create a second Cloud Storage bucket in the same region and split the objects between the two buckets
Move the origin application to a machine type with more vCPUs, to shorten the processing time of each request

stem: A retailer sees its monthly Google Cloud bill jump in the middle of the month. Finance wants to know which products, SKUs and resources caused the change, and the platform team would like the explanation to appear without someone starting an investigation each time. Which capability fits best?

choices.text: Gemini Cloud Assist cost anomaly analysis, which runs when an anomaly is detected and explains the change behind it
Gemini Cloud Assist IAM assistance, which proposes narrower roles for the users who created the extra resources
Gemini Cloud Assist code troubleshooting, which traces a Cloud Run error down to its cause in the code
Gemini Cloud Assist natural language design, which helps create a new and cheaper architecture for the application

stem: Cymbal Retail's product page calls a recommendation service to show "you may also like" items. When that service is slow or fails, the whole page fails and shoppers cannot buy the product they came for. The business says recommendations are nice to have, and the checkout is the revenue. Which design change best follows reliability guidance?

choices.text: Retry the recommendation call repeatedly until it succeeds, so the page always shows the complete content to every shopper
Remove recommendations from the site, because any optional dependency lowers the availability of the page
Raise the availability target of the recommendation service to equal checkout, and keep the page dependent on it
Add a short timeout and a circuit breaker to the recommendation call, and show the page without it on failure

stem: A hospital group runs a patient-scheduling application whose database is read-heavy: about 90% of queries are lookups and reports, and writes come from one region. At peak, the single Cloud SQL primary reaches its CPU limit, although the team does not want to rewrite the application or change database engines. Which approach scales the workload with the least change?

choices.text: Disable high availability on the primary, because the standby consumes CPU that the primary needs for queries
Add Cloud SQL read replicas, and route read-only queries and reports to them while writes continue to go to the primary
Migrate the database to a globally distributed Spanner instance, and rewrite the schema and queries for the new engine
Move all report queries into the primary's maintenance window, so that they no longer compete with lookups during peak hours

stem: An application is deployed in two regions, each with a managed instance group behind its own regional load balancer. Users reach it through a DNS name that points to the primary region, and operators change the DNS record manually if that region fails. During a recent regional outage some users kept reaching the failed region for more than an hour because resolvers cached the old record. What design change gives the fastest automatic fail-over?

choices.text: Add a third regional load balancer in the primary region, giving users more entry points into the failed region
Lower the DNS record's time-to-live to one second and keep the manual process for changing the record when needed
Use a global external Application Load Balancer with health-checked backends in both regions
Add more instances to the managed instance group in the primary region before the next outage occurs, to hold more load

stem: A warm-standby disaster recovery design replicates data to a second region and keeps only a few VMs running there. During a rehearsal, scaling up the standby stack to production size failed in the recovery region because the required machine type was temporarily unavailable in the chosen zone, and the RTO was missed. What should the architect add to the design?

choices.text: Reservations for the required Compute Engine capacity in the recovery region, so resources are available when failover starts
A larger boot disk for the standby VM image, so that the machine starts faster after the failover begins
A second storage bucket in the primary region for the VM images, so the images are available if the first bucket fails
A shorter health check interval on the primary region, so that the failure is detected sooner than it is now

stem: A broadcaster stores newly produced footage in a Cloud Storage dual-region bucket for a production tool that must continue after a regional outage. The business sets a recovery point objective of 15 minutes for newly written objects across both regions, and default replication targets are too slow for that. What should the architect enable?

choices.text: The Archive storage class, which stores each object in colder storage that costs less for long-term retention
A retention policy on the bucket, which prevents any object from being deleted or replaced before a set age
Turbo replication on the dual-region bucket, designed to copy new objects to both regions within 15 minutes
Object Versioning on the bucket, keeping older versions of overwritten or deleted objects in the bucket

stem: An e-commerce company has a user-facing Cloud Run service that runs a heavy framework. After periods without traffic, the first visitors wait several seconds for a response while a new instance starts, which violates the latency target for the first request. Costs for always running the service on VMs are not acceptable. Which change best fits the performance and cost goals?

choices.text: Rebuild the service on Compute Engine VMs with fixed capacity, because serverless platforms cannot meet a latency target
Set a minimum number of instances so a warm one is always ready, with autoscaling for bursts above it
Increase the request timeout of the service so the first visitor can wait for the instance to start
Disable autoscaling and set the maximum number of instances to one, so no new instances are started during traffic bursts

stem: EHR Healthcare must leave its colocation facility because the lease ends in about ten months. It has a few hundred servers, documentation of its applications is thin, and several are tied to on-premises insurer integrations. What is the best first step in the migration plan?

choices.text: Renew the lease for three more years, since applications with unknown dependencies cannot be moved safely at all
Re-architect every application into microservices before moving anything, so the whole estate is cloud-native on arrival at Google Cloud
Start moving servers in alphabetical order so the project shows progress, and rewrite the documentation in parallel
Use Migration Center discovery and assessment to inventory servers, map dependencies and decide which workloads must move together

stem: A manufacturer has a spreadsheet with outdated server lists and no idea which servers talk to which. It wants an automated inventory, a view of application and network dependencies, a recommendation of target Google Cloud products and a cost comparison that follows its own preferences, such as target region and commitment term. Which choice meets this?

choices.text: Create a Compute Engine VM for each listed server, so that actual usage can be measured after the VMs are running
Use Cloud Monitoring dashboards on the Google Cloud projects, because they show resource usage across the estate
Use Migration Center discovery, then assessment with dependency analysis, fit assessment and TCO reports
Hire a team to interview application owners, because only people know how systems relate to each other

stem: Which TWO situations point to a rehost (lift and shift) as the most suitable migration approach for a workload? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The team wants to use fully managed services and horizontal scalability that the current design cannot use
A hard exit date is close and the workload can run in the target environment as it is, with minimal changes
The business wants to remove technical debt and move a monolith to independent services that scale separately
The current application is not supported on Google Cloud and the business wants to build a cloud-optimized replacement
The workload is packaged vendor software whose code cannot be changed and which cannot be retired yet

stem: A company has finished planning a migration of about 120 applications. The migration team has little experience with the landing zone, the network connection and the cutover runbooks. Which application should the architect choose for the first migration wave?

choices.text: A low-criticality application with few dependencies and simple data, to validate the platform and runbooks
The application on the oldest operating system, because it is the one with the highest security exposure
The most business-critical application, since a success there proves the approach to the whole company immediately
The application with the most dependencies, because it will reveal every integration problem in one single step

stem: A retailer plans to connect its data center, which uses 10.0.0.0/8 addresses in many sites, to a new Google Cloud environment with Cloud VPN and Interconnect. Network planning is still open. Before creating subnets, which action avoids a routing problem that is hard to fix later?

choices.text: Create the VPC subnets from 10.0.0.0/8, matching the on-premises ranges, so that workloads keep their addresses
Postpone address planning until the connections are up, since routes can be advertised in either direction later on
Use public IP addresses for all migrated VMs, so private range overlaps with the data center no longer matter
Define an IP plan giving Google Cloud subnets ranges that do not overlap with on-premises or other connected networks

stem: KnightMotives moved the web front end of its build-to-order system to Google Cloud while the mainframe ERP stayed on premises. Each page now makes dozens of sequential calls to the ERP over the hybrid link, and dealers report very slow pages even though the link has plenty of bandwidth. What should the migration plan have used to prevent this?

choices.text: Dependency mapping, to move chatty components in one wave or add an API layer or cache that cuts cross-link calls
A switch of the front end to Spot VMs, so that its compute is less expensive while it waits for the ERP responses
A plan that moves each tier in its own wave, starting with whichever tier is the easiest for the team
A larger Interconnect capacity, because slow pages in hybrid designs are always caused by too little bandwidth

stem: A company will move database servers running software that is licensed per physical core. It holds eligible licenses and wants to reuse them on Google Cloud, and the vendor requires that the licensed cores be tracked on dedicated physical hardware. Which approach should the architect plan?

choices.text: Replace the database software with a SaaS product during the migration, because licenses cannot be reused on any public cloud
Buy the largest available machine type, so that the vendor audit finds more cores than the licensing requires
Run them on sole-tenant nodes, which dedicate physical hosts and show physical core usage for bring-your-own-license
Run them on standard multi-tenant Compute Engine VMs and send the vendor the VM sizes, because core counts are the same

stem: A finance team builds the business case for moving a data center workload to Google Cloud. The steady-state monthly cloud cost looks lower than the current run cost. Which TWO cost items should the plan add so the case is not overstated? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The savings expected from a future rewrite of the application, counted as a benefit of the lift and shift
The list price of every cloud service for the full term, before any usage or sizing information is applied to it
The purchase price of on-premises hardware that was bought years ago and has already been paid for
One-time migration effort such as assessment, tooling, data transfer, testing, retraining and any application changes
The period in which both the on-premises environment and the migrated environment run in parallel until cutover is complete

stem: The discovery data for a planned migration shows that many virtual machines have 16 vCPUs allocated but averaged under 10% CPU usage over the last three months. The team proposes to create each target VM with exactly the allocated size so that the migration is simple. What should the architect advise?

choices.text: Ignore sizing during migration, because Compute Engine bills only the CPU that is actually used by the guest operating system
Size targets from measured utilization plus peak headroom, and review them after migration
Keep the allocated sizes, because reducing sizes is a risk that should wait until application owners approve it
Choose the smallest possible machine for every VM, regardless of the measured peaks, to maximize savings from the first day

stem: A team has completed the cutover of a customer-facing database to Google Cloud over a weekend. To save money, a manager proposes powering off and wiping the old on-premises servers on Monday morning. Which TWO elements should the migration plan include instead? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Agree measurable rollback triggers before cutover, such as error rate or data mismatch, and name who decides
Delete the source only after the cloud bill for the first month has been reviewed by the finance department
Keep the source environment running permanently, because decommissioning always carries too much risk to attempt
Wipe the servers immediately, because a rollback plan indicates a lack of confidence in the migration
Keep the source intact and in sync for a defined stabilization period, with rollback criteria, then decommission

stem: Before the first migration wave, a company's cloud team has the migration tooling ready but no organization structure, network connectivity, identity setup or central logging in Google Cloud. The team lead wants to begin moving servers now and fix the foundation as problems appear. What should the architect recommend?

choices.text: Let each application team build its own organization structure, networks and logging, to avoid waiting for a central design
Build the landing zone first: resource hierarchy, IAM, network and hybrid connectivity, logging and monitoring, then migrate into it
Move the servers into a single project in the default network and add structure later, since projects can be reorganized at any time without any impact
Pause server migration until all applications have been modernized, so that nothing needs a foundation designed for legacy servers

stem: Discovery of a company's estate shows 400 virtual machines. About 60 of them have had near-zero CPU use for six months, receive no inbound connections according to the dependency data and have no named owner. How should the migration plan treat them?

choices.text: Shut them down permanently on the same day, because the data shows that nobody uses them at all
Rehost them to the smallest machine type and leave them there indefinitely, to be reviewed in the next budget year
Confirm with owners whether they are still needed, and retire those that are not instead of migrating them
Migrate all of them in the first wave, since carrying unused servers is cheaper than asking owners questions

stem: A consulting firm brings in 30 short-term contractors who must edit and run infrastructure scripts against a client's Google Cloud projects for six weeks. Contractor laptops cannot be managed by the client, and the client wants no local installation of tools and no source files left on personal machines. The security team also wants to control the machine image, the machine size and the network the environments attach to. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: Give each contractor a Cloud Shell session, since its pre-configured VM image, machine size and network can be fixed by the client's administrators in every project
Create one shared Compute Engine VM and give all contractors the same SSH account, so that one machine holds every script and every credential
Ask each contractor to install the Google Cloud CLI locally and run every script from the laptop with a long-lived service account key stored in a file
Define Cloud Workstations configurations with the image, machine type, network and persistent home, and let each contractor create a workstation from them

stem: Altostrat Media runs its recommendation and transcoding services on GKE and its event tasks on Cloud Run. Its developers currently build container images by hand, write Kubernetes YAML in a text editor, and wait for a pipeline run to see whether a change works. The platform lead wants a faster inner loop from the developers' own IDEs: run and debug the application against a cluster, and get help with Kubernetes and Skaffold configuration. Which tool should the architect recommend?

choices.text: A Terraform module that creates a new GKE cluster per developer, so that each developer edits the same YAML files in a plain text editor
Cloud Deploy for each developer, because its release pipelines can replace the need to run and debug the application from the IDE
Cloud Code in the developers' IDEs, which provides run and debug against Kubernetes and Cloud Run, sample templates and YAML and Skaffold editing support
The Google Cloud console's workload pages, which let developers edit deployed Kubernetes resources directly in the production cluster for fast feedback

stem: A team builds a service on Spanner and wants fast, free tests that run on every commit in a CI job, without creating Spanner instances or credentials for the job. Which TWO statements correctly describe how to use, and what to expect from, the Spanner emulator? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Treat a green run on the emulator as proof of production performance, because the emulator reproduces production throughput and latency
Run the emulator in the CI job and point the client library at it, accepting that data, schema and configuration are lost on restart
Use the emulator as a low-cost production database for small tenants, because it offers the same APIs as the Spanner service
Run the emulator in a shared long-lived container so that schemas created in one commit are guaranteed to still exist for the next
Keep an additional test stage against a real Spanner instance, because error messages and checks such as whether a statement is partitionable can differ from production

stem: A developer follows a tutorial for the Pub/Sub emulator. The application, built with a Cloud Client Library, now publishes messages locally as expected after the PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST environment variable is set. The developer then tries to inspect the emulator's topics with a gcloud pubsub command and with the Google Cloud console, but neither shows any topic. What is the correct understanding?

choices.text: The emulator did not start correctly, so the developer must reinstall the Google Cloud CLI before topics can be created or displayed
The emulator creates topics in a hidden project, so the developer should grant the Pub/Sub Viewer role on that project to see them
The emulator keeps topics only for 60 seconds, so the developer should republish and run the gcloud command before they expire
The emulator is reached through the client libraries' environment variable only, and it does not support the console or gcloud pubsub commands

stem: A team designs tests for a service that stores time-series data in Bigtable and wants to use the Bigtable emulator in its test suite. Which statement about what the emulator offers is correct?

choices.text: Data is kept only in memory, and a test can connect with any project and instance name, then create the tables and data it needs on every run
The emulator provides administrative APIs for creating and managing instances and clusters, which tests can call to build a production-like topology
The emulator encrypts traffic with TLS and enforces IAM, so security configuration can be validated end to end on a developer machine
Data written to the emulator is replicated to a second local node, so failover behavior of a multi-cluster instance can be tested

stem: A team writes integration tests for an application that uses the Firestore server client library. The tests must never touch production data, must run on developer laptops and in CI without any Google Cloud credentials, and the team does not want test-only branches in the application code. What is the best design?

choices.text: Start the Firestore emulator in the test environment and set FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST, so the unchanged client library connects to it
Create a separate Firestore database in the production project, prefix all test document paths with "test_", and delete them after each run
Add a configuration flag in the application that, in test mode, swaps the Firestore client for a hand-written in-memory fake class
Run the tests against the production database with a read-only service account key kept in the CI system

stem: EHR Healthcare is moving from its colocation data center and expects to create several nearly identical environments (development, test, per-region production) for its containerized platform, with differences only in names, sizes and network ranges. Past outages came from misconfiguration. The architect wants repeatable, reviewable provisioning that a new region can reuse. Which approach is best?

choices.text: Document the build steps in a wiki, let each regional team follow them in the console, and then verify the result with a checklist
Write reusable Terraform modules in version control and have each environment call them with its own values via a reviewed plan
Clone the production project's resources into each new environment by hand, then edit names, sizes and ranges directly in each copy
Write one large shell script of gcloud commands per environment and run it from an engineer's workstation whenever a new region is needed

stem: A company manages production with Terraform, but an incident review finds that several firewall rules and a machine type were changed by hand in the console during earlier incidents. The next terraform apply would silently revert some of those changes. Which TWO measures best prevent configuration drift from recurring while still letting on-call engineers act quickly? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Give every engineer the Admin basic role in production so that urgent console fixes are never blocked and later get written back to the code
Delete the Terraform state after each incident so that the next apply starts from a clean picture of production
Stop using the Terraform plan step and apply directly, so differences are corrected immediately without waiting for a review
Restrict write permissions in production to the CI/CD service account, and give people break-glass access with auditing, so emergency changes are rare, visible and backported to the code
Run terraform plan on a schedule and on every pipeline run, and treat any unexpected difference as a finding to import into the code or revert

stem: Cymbal Retail manages its Cloud SQL for MySQL order database with Terraform. During a refactor an engineer renames the resource block in the configuration. The plan output shows the existing database instance would be destroyed and a new one created. Reviewers almost approved the plan because the pipeline summary only reported "1 to add, 1 to destroy". Which change best protects the architect's stateful resources in the future?

choices.text: Disable plan output in the pipeline so that reviewers focus on code diffs instead of tool output that they may misread
Remove the database from Terraform so nobody can destroy it by accident, and manage it by hand in the console
Enable deletion protection on databases, have reviewers read destroy lines in the plan, and use a state move for renames
Add a post-apply script that restores the latest backup when a database disappears, so a destroyed instance is recreated automatically

stem: A company runs an order service on Cloud Run and a batch job on Compute Engine. Developers also test locally. Which TWO practices follow Google Cloud's recommendations for authenticating these workloads to Google APIs? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Download a key file for the Compute Engine default service account, store it in the repository and read it from GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS in every environment
Have the production applications use developers' personal user credentials, since these are always the most traceable identity for audit
Create a user-managed service account for each workload, grant it only the roles it needs, and attach it to the Cloud Run service or VM so that the client library finds credentials automatically
Hardcode a long-lived access token in the application's configuration file and refresh it by hand every few months
Use Application Default Credentials in the code, so that the same code uses the attached service account in production and local credentials during development

stem: Altostrat Media's legacy content-ingestion systems stay on premises for now. They run in a data center whose identity provider supports OpenID Connect. These servers must upload objects to Cloud Storage and call other Google Cloud APIs. The security team forbids downloading service account keys. Which approach should the architect choose?

choices.text: Make a single Google user account for the ingestion team and let the servers sign in with its stored password through a script
Set up Workload Identity Federation with the on-premises OIDC provider and let client libraries use its configuration file via ADC
Create one service account key per ingestion server and rotate the key files every 90 days with a scheduled job
Open the buckets to allUsers write access from the data center's public IP range, so the servers need no credentials at all

stem: A new team will build a Python service that publishes to Pub/Sub, writes to Cloud Storage and calls other Google Cloud APIs. A senior developer proposes writing REST calls by hand with a generic HTTP library and managing OAuth tokens in the application. Another proposes the older Google API Client Libraries because "they cover every API". What should the architect recommend?

choices.text: Cloud Client Libraries, which handle authentication and can use gRPC, with the older libraries only where a Cloud library is missing
The Google API Client Libraries for all new code, because they are the newer model and support gRPC for the highest throughput
Hand-written REST calls, because only they allow complete control of retries and authentication across all Google Cloud services
A single in-house wrapper over raw HTTP, so that every team shares one custom client and the company avoids vendor-provided libraries

stem: An operations team has years of shell runbooks that copy and sync data to Cloud Storage with gsutil, and is about to write ten new automation scripts for large object transfers. The architect is asked which command-line tool the new scripts should use. What is the best advice?

choices.text: Stop using command-line tools and copy objects through the console's upload dialog, since this scales better for large transfers
Replace the scripts with the bq command-line tool, because bq is the command-line tool intended for managing Cloud Storage objects
Keep gsutil for all new scripts, because it is the only tool that supports bucket and object operations for Cloud Storage
Write the new scripts with gcloud storage, which Google recommends over the legacy gsutil, and migrate the old runbooks over time

stem: A developer signs in to the Google Cloud CLI on a laptop with a user account, and gcloud commands work. The developer then runs a locally developed Python application that uses a Cloud Client Library, and it fails with an error that no Application Default Credentials could be found. What explains this, and what is the right fix?

choices.text: The CLI login and ADC use separate credentials, so the developer should run gcloud auth application-default login rather than copy a key file
The gcloud login expired, so the developer should download a service account key and set it in the code as a string
Cloud Client Libraries cannot run outside Google Cloud, so the application can only be tested after deployment to Cloud Run
The user account lacks the Owner role, so the developer should be granted Owner on the project for libraries to find credentials

stem: A product team wants its public mobile app to read a Google Cloud API that returns non-sensitive reference data. An engineer suggests embedding a standard API key in the app because it is simple. A second engineer wants to use that key to let the backend job write to Cloud Storage as the application's identity. What should the architect advise?

choices.text: Avoid keys in every case, because they cannot be restricted and always give full access to the project
Use the same API key for both, because a key authenticates a principal and IAM roles can be granted to it
Use the API key for the backend job and a service account for the mobile app, since keys are safer on client devices
A key only identifies the project for quota, not a principal, so the backend job should use a service account via ADC

stem: A team uses Terraform to create a VM and, in the same configuration, runs a shell script through a provisioner that calls gcloud to create a Pub/Sub topic and a firewall rule. Later the topic is deleted by someone, and a terraform plan shows no difference. A reviewer asks the architect what the design problem is. What is the best answer?

choices.text: Pub/Sub topics are always excluded from IaC for reliability reasons and must be managed through the console
Terraform cannot create Pub/Sub topics or firewall rules, so scripts are the only supported way to manage those resources
Script-created resources are outside Terraform state, so changes go undetected; declare them as Terraform resources
The plan output is wrong whenever a provisioner exists, so the team should apply twice to be sure

stem: Cymbal Retail publishes a shared Terraform module for a regional storefront stack. Teams call it for development, test and each production region. A review finds that the module gives its project_id variable a default that points at the production project, and a team that forgot to set it deployed test resources there. The module also exposes a variable for every possible setting. Which change follows Google's Terraform guidance best?

choices.text: Keep the production default so deployments always succeed, and ask teams to read the README before they change the value
Remove the default from environment-specific variables such as project_id so callers must supply them, and expose only values that really vary
Hardcode the project inside the module and publish one copy of the module per environment, so that no variable is needed at all
Give every variable, including project_id, a default of an empty string, so that the module never fails when a caller omits a value

stem: KnightMotives plans a large hybrid cloud program with new platforms, a data management platform and a simulation environment. Its teams have little experience operating Google Cloud, and leadership asks how the architect would make sure the new platforms can be run well once they go live. Which approach follows the operational excellence pillar?

choices.text: Concentrate on selecting tools first and leave roles, runbooks and service levels to be defined by each team after go-live
Plan readiness across workforce skills, processes such as observability and incidents, supporting tooling, and governance such as service levels
Defer all operational planning until the first major outage shows which procedures are missing, and then write them
Hire an external provider to run everything permanently and avoid building internal skills, since operations adds no business value

stem: A SaaS company is writing the operations plan for a new customer-facing service. Which TWO actions follow the operational excellence pillar's recommendations to ensure operational readiness and performance? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Define SLOs that are specific, measurable and time-bound, and track them with service level indicators in Cloud Monitoring
State the objective as "the service should be fast and reliable" and review it only when customers complain about it
Run performance tests only after the first peak sales event shows whether the service copes
Skip capacity planning because autoscaling removes the need to forecast demand or quotas
Run load and stress tests regularly to find bottlenecks before peak load, and use the results to tune capacity and configuration

stem: After a two-hour outage caused by an expired certificate, the engineering manager wants a post-incident review. Several engineers worry that the review will be used to assign blame to the person who missed the renewal. Which approach follows Google Cloud's operational excellence guidance?

choices.text: Assign the incident to the person who owned the certificate and add the outage to their annual review, so accountability is clear
Skip the review and only renew the certificate to fix the symptom, since further analysis of a solved incident wastes engineering time
Skip the review for incidents shorter than one working day, and only analyze outages that exceed the contractual SLA
Run a blameless post-incident review for root cause and lessons learned, and turn findings into actions such as automated renewal and expiry alerts

stem: A company's operations team spends most of its week on manual tasks: creating projects and networks from tickets, patching servers by hand, and deploying releases by copying files. Releases are slow and often differ between environments. The architect is asked which changes best apply the operational excellence pillar's guidance on automating and managing change. Which is best?

choices.text: Hire additional administrators, so that the same manual procedures are completed sooner by more people
Freeze all changes outside a quarterly window, so that fewer manual tasks are needed during the rest of the year
Adopt infrastructure as code in version control, CI/CD with Cloud Build and Cloud Deploy, and configuration management for patching
Let each team write its own deployment scripts and keep them on laptops, so changes are fast because no review is required

stem: A ticketing company expects its web traffic to grow tenfold during the ticket release of a famous tour in nine months. The service runs on managed instance groups with autoscaling, behind a load balancer, with a regional database. The team lead says "autoscaling will handle it." Which action best reflects the operational excellence guidance?

choices.text: Rely on autoscaling alone, since adding instances automatically covers any increase in load without prior planning, quota checks or testing
Forecast demand, check quotas, load test at the expected peak well ahead of the event, and fix the bottlenecks found, including the database
Wait for the event and increase limits by contacting support only if errors occur during the release
Provision ten times the current capacity permanently from today and disable autoscaling to keep the architecture simple

stem: EHR Healthcare will run containerized applications in several Kubernetes environments, including a few in Google Cloud projects of different teams. Compliance needs consistent log retention, and the security team wants one place to search logs across all projects, while individual teams still need to see their own project's logs. What should the architect design?

choices.text: Disable logging in project-level buckets so entries exist only in a central project, and give each team the Owner role there
Ask each team to export its logs weekly to a spreadsheet, and set a reminder to merge them for the auditors
Set the highest retention on every project's _Default bucket and have the security team request access to each project when needed
Create an organization-level aggregated sink to a central project's log bucket with the required retention, leaving project buckets in place

stem: Cymbal Retail is modernizing its storefront into several microservices on Kubernetes. Customers report that checkout is sometimes slow, but each service's average latency looks normal on its dashboard, and the team cannot tell which downstream call is responsible for individual slow requests. Which tool should the architect add first?

choices.text: Cloud Trace, instrumented in the services, to follow single requests across services and see which call adds the delay
Uptime checks from several regions, which show the time each microservice spends calling its dependencies
Cloud Profiler alone, because it shows the end-to-end latency of every request across all services in one timeline view
Log-based metrics that count error entries, because slowness is always visible as an error log entry

stem: A Java service on GKE uses high CPU all day, so the team's compute bill is rising. No single request is slow, load tests in the lab do not reproduce the pattern, and nobody knows which functions consume the CPU. The team lead is wary of any tool that slows production noticeably. Which approach is best?

choices.text: Run a one-time microbenchmark of the service in a staging cluster and optimize whatever the benchmark highlights first
Enable verbose debug logging in all pods and read the log volume to guess which functions are expensive
Add the Cloud Profiler agent and review its continuous production CPU and heap profiles, which map usage to source code at low overhead
Add more nodes until CPU utilization falls below the alert threshold, then reconsider the code later

stem: A payments team's alerting policies fire when any single VM exceeds 70% CPU for one minute. On-call engineers get dozens of pages per week, most of which require no action, while a recent real outage (checkout errors for 20 minutes) paged no one. They want alerting that reflects customer impact and reduces noise. Which TWO changes should the architect make? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Send every alert, including low-urgency ones, to the same pager channel so that nothing can be overlooked by anyone
Disable alerting during business hours, and rely on customers to report problems to the support desk
Define a checkout success SLO and alert on its error-budget burn rate with a fast-burn and a slow-burn policy
Lower every threshold to 50% CPU and shorten the retest window to 30 seconds, so alerts fire earlier
Page on user-visible symptoms and keep cause-level signals such as per-VM CPU for dashboards or non-urgent notifications, and use retest windows long enough to avoid firing on a single spike

stem: A company promises its enterprise customers 99.9% availability for a public HTTPS API on Google Cloud. Internal metrics show healthy servers, yet a regional DNS problem recently made the API unreachable for some customers without any internal error. The operations lead wants an independent view of availability from the customers' perspective, with an alert when the API cannot be reached. What should the architect add?

choices.text: A log-based metric on the application logs, because requests that never reach the application are still logged by it
A weekly manual test by an engineer from the office network, recorded in a spreadsheet
A CPU utilization alert on the backend instances, because high CPU is always the first sign of an unreachable API
A public uptime check that probes the API endpoint from multiple world locations, with an alerting policy on failures

stem: A company links its on-premises network to one VPC network through HA VPN, with a Cloud Router in us-central1. The VPC network has subnets in us-central1 and europe-west1, and the VPC network uses its default dynamic routing mode. On-premises routers learn the us-central1 subnets only, so servers cannot reach the europe-west1 VMs over the tunnels. What is the correct fix?

choices.text: Increase the number of tunnels in us-central1 to four, so that the extra capacity lets the Cloud Router announce more subnets
Change the dynamic routing mode of the VPC network to global, so the Cloud Router advertises and learns routes for all regions
Create a second pair of HA VPN tunnels in europe-west1 that use static routes, because BGP can only cover one region per network
Add an ingress firewall rule that allows the on-premises ranges to reach the europe-west1 subnets, since the firewall is dropping the traffic

stem: A security team must block exploit attempts and command-and-control traffic between application VMs that sit in the same VPC network, inspecting the packets inline rather than only raising alerts, and it wants a Google-managed service instead of running virtual appliances. Which configuration achieves this?

choices.text: Create zonal Cloud NGFW firewall endpoints, a threat-prevention security profile group, and firewall policy rules that apply that group
Place Cloud Armor with a managed rule set in front of the workloads so that east-west traffic is filtered by web rules
Add VPC firewall deny rules for the IP ranges of known attackers, and refresh the list manually each week from threat reports
Enable Cloud IDS with an IDS endpoint and packet mirroring policy, so that every detected threat is blocked at the VM before it spreads

stem: A platform team lets many developers edit VM settings in shared development projects. Firewall rules currently permit database access only from VMs that carry the network tag "web". An audit finds that any developer who can edit an instance can add that tag and reach the database. The team wants rules keyed to a workload label that only a security group can assign. What should it change?

choices.text: Move the database VMs to a separate zone, because firewall rules are evaluated per zone and developers cannot cross it
Keep network tags but add a naming convention for tags, and ask developers to document every tag they apply in the ticket system
Use secure tags in network firewall policy rules as sources and targets, and grant the permission to bind them only to the security group
Replace the tag rule with one based on the web subnet range, since instance editors cannot change a subnet range assignment

stem: An online game studio runs UDP game servers on Compute Engine VMs in one region. The servers must see each player's original source IP address for anti-cheat checks, the load balancer should not terminate the player traffic, and the studio wants high throughput without a proxy layer. Which load balancer configuration fits?

choices.text: An internal passthrough Network Load Balancer with a regional forwarding rule, so that players reach it through a private address
A regional external passthrough Network Load Balancer with a backend service and a UDP forwarding rule
A global external Application Load Balancer with a URL map, to terminate connections near players
A global external proxy Network Load Balancer, because TCP proxying lets the servers choose the source address they see

stem: EHR Healthcare runs an internal eligibility API used by application tiers in two regions, and the service must stay available if a whole region fails. The API must not be reachable from the internet, and clients should use a single DNS name no matter where they run, without manual switching. Which load balancer fits?

choices.text: A cross-region internal Application Load Balancer with backend instance groups in both regions behind one backend service
An internal passthrough Network Load Balancer in each region, with clients switching to the other address by hand during an outage
A regional external Application Load Balancer restricted by firewall rules to the two regions' NAT addresses
A regional internal Application Load Balancer with global access enabled, with all backends placed in the closest region

stem: A company will connect a new VPC network to on-premises networks and to a partner network through VPC Network Peering. It wants control over which regions receive subnets and which address ranges are used. Which TWO reasons support creating the VPC network in custom mode instead of auto mode? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Custom mode is the only mode that supports Cloud Router, so hybrid connectivity cannot be configured on auto mode
Custom mode removes the implied deny-ingress rule, so peered networks can reach every VM
Custom mode is the only mode that can host Private Google Access for subnets in several regions
Custom mode lets the team choose non-overlapping ranges, which avoids conflicts with on-premises and peered networks
Custom mode creates subnets only in the regions the team chooses, so unused regions get no subnet and no address space

stem: A data-science team runs a large analytics workload on another cloud provider and must exchange tens of gigabits of data with Google Cloud privately. The team does not want to deploy its own network equipment in a colocation facility, and it wants a physical link between the two clouds that Google provisions. Which connectivity should it choose?

choices.text: HA VPN tunnels across the public internet between a Google Cloud Cloud Router and a virtual gateway of the other cloud
Partner Interconnect through a carrier, where the team orders the circuits and the other cloud's connection separately
Cross-Cloud Interconnect, where Google provisions a dedicated link to the other provider's network
Direct Peering at a Google edge location, which allows the two clouds' traffic to be exchanged without using the internet

stem: Cymbal Retail's catalog service runs on a private GKE cluster whose nodes have no external IP addresses. Suppliers will let the service call their APIs only from a fixed set of public IP addresses that Cymbal must give them in advance. Which configuration meets this?

choices.text: Cloud Router custom route advertisements that announce the supplier IP ranges into the VPC network
A Cloud NAT gateway in the cluster's region that uses reserved static external IP addresses for the node and Pod ranges
Private Google Access on the subnet, so that all outbound connections leave through Google's own address blocks
An ephemeral external IP address on each node, with the supplier allowlist updated whenever autoscaling adds a node

stem: A company runs Active Directory DNS on premises for corp.example and uses Cloud DNS for the private zone gcp.corp.example in a VPC network connected by Cloud Interconnect. On-premises servers must resolve names in gcp.corp.example, and Compute Engine VMs must resolve names in corp.example. What should be configured?

choices.text: A hosts file distributed to every VM and server, refreshed from a script when names change
A secondary zone on the on-premises DNS servers, with the VMs configured manually to use the Active Directory servers' addresses
A public Cloud DNS zone for both names, with on-premises servers and VMs resolving them over the internet
An inbound server policy for on-premises queries, and a Cloud DNS forwarding zone for corp.example that targets the on-premises servers

stem: KnightMotives connects a plant to Google Cloud with Dedicated Interconnect for real-time analytics and keeps an HA VPN as a backup. Both paths advertise the same on-premises prefixes through Cloud Router. The network team sees traffic spread across both, and VPN latency is hurting real-time workloads. How should it make the Interconnect the preferred path and the VPN a standby?

choices.text: Give the Interconnect session a lower priority value than the VPN session, so the VPN carries traffic only if Interconnect routes disappear
Give the Interconnect session a higher priority number than the VPN session, since larger values mean higher preference in Cloud Router
Give both BGP sessions the same advertised route priority so that the Cloud Router balances traffic equally between them
Delete the VPN tunnels and rely on the two Interconnect VLAN attachments only, to keep the routing table simple

stem: Altostrat Media is modernizing in steps. Its on-premises ingestion API stays in the data center for now, while new services run in GKE. The team wants one public hostname and one global external Application Load Balancer, with the ingest path sent to the on-premises servers over the existing Cloud Interconnect. What backend configuration does this require?

choices.text: An internet network endpoint group with the data center's public hostname, so that requests travel across the public internet
A serverless network endpoint group pointing to the on-premises servers, because it can reference any reachable endpoint
A managed instance group whose template defines on-premises servers, kept in sync by the autoscaler
A hybrid connectivity network endpoint group holding the on-premises IP:port endpoints, used as a backend and routed by the URL map

stem: A security architect needs to detect lateral movement between VMs in the same subnets, including intra-subnet traffic. Production traffic must not be placed in the data path of the inspection engine, and the team wants to act on the findings later. Which TWO elements belong in the design? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A policy that makes Cloud IDS drop malicious packets inline, so that it stops threats without any other control
A single IDS endpoint in one region that inspects mirrored traffic for every region by default
Cloud IDS findings used to drive follow-up action through Cloud NGFW, because Cloud IDS alerts but does not block
A Cloud Armor policy on the VPC network, because Cloud Armor inspects subnet traffic between VMs
A Cloud IDS endpoint in each region that holds monitored VMs, with packet mirroring policies that select the VMs or subnets to inspect

stem: A team runs a Cloud Run service that must read from a Memorystore instance and call an internal API in a connected on-premises network, both through private IP addresses. The team wants to avoid running and sizing connector instances and wants the best throughput. Which configuration should it use?

choices.text: Direct VPC egress, with the service attached to a VPC network and subnet that has enough free addresses for its instances
Serverless VPC Access connectors with the largest connector instance type, so that throughput is no longer limited
A move to GKE Autopilot, since Cloud Run cannot send traffic to internal IP addresses at all
A public IP address for the Memorystore instance, secured with an allowlist of Cloud Run's outbound addresses

stem: A company exposes a Cloud Run service to customers through a global external Application Load Balancer so that it can use Cloud Armor and a custom domain. A security review finds that the default run.app URL still accepts requests from the internet, bypassing Cloud Armor. What should the architect configure?

choices.text: Add a firewall rule on the VPC network that blocks the run.app domain's IP addresses from internet clients
Set the ingress to internal and Cloud Load Balancing, and use a serverless NEG as the load balancer backend
Remove the serverless NEG backend and send customers directly to the run.app URL, protecting it with IAM only
Place the service behind a Cloud NAT gateway so that inbound traffic from the internet is translated first

stem: A team runs a nightly image-processing job on Compute Engine VMs and wants to use Spot VMs to reduce cost. Each task takes up to forty minutes, tasks can be repeated safely, and the job can finish late. Which TWO design choices make it work well on Spot VMs? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Run workers in a managed instance group built from a Spot instance template so the group recreates preempted instances as capacity returns
Run the job queue and the coordinator on Spot VMs too, so that every component receives the same discount
Enable automatic restart and live migration on the workers so Spot preemption is transparent to the job
Rely on a maximum 24-hour runtime for Spot VMs so tasks are never interrupted
Save progress to Cloud Storage regularly and use a shutdown script to react to the preemption notice

stem: KnightMotives runs hundreds of VMware virtual machines in a data center that is being closed. Their IP addresses are hard-coded in plant systems, the operations team is trained on vSphere, and the move must be done in waves with little downtime. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: Convert each VM to a Compute Engine instance, then change its address and update every plant system that points to it
Use VMware Engine and migrate in waves with VMware HCX, extending the networks so VMs keep their IP addresses
Rewrite the applications as containers on GKE first, and migrate only after every VM has been replaced
Export the VMs as files to Cloud Storage nightly, and restart them on Compute Engine when the data center closes

stem: EHR Healthcare must create several consistent environments for development, staging and production, plus a new isolated environment for each large hospital customer. Engineers need reviewed, repeatable changes, and the old Deployment Manager templates can no longer be used. Which approach should the architect adopt?

choices.text: Continued use of the existing Deployment Manager templates, since a completed deployment keeps working indefinitely
Shell scripts of gcloud commands run from Cloud Shell, adjusted by each engineer before each environment is created
Terraform in Git deployed through Infrastructure Manager, with one deployment per environment and different input variables
Environments created through the console by following a runbook, with screenshots stored as the record of the configuration

stem: A company runs about 600 Linux and Windows VMs across several zones. Security wants OS patches applied on a recurring schedule, with limits on how many VMs in a zone are patched at once, and a report of which VMs are missing patches. What should the architect set up?

choices.text: Unattended automatic updates on every operating system image, relying on each vendor's own default schedule
A Cloud Build trigger that logs in to each VM over SSH on the first of the month and runs update commands
A cron script on each VM that runs a package update and writes results to a local file for the team to read
VM Manager patch management with scheduled patch deployments, zone-by-zone rollout and compliance reporting

stem: A web tier runs in a regional managed instance group behind a load balancer. Today administrators patch running VMs in place, so instances slowly drift apart and some fail health checks after patching. The team wants consistent, low-risk updates without downtime. What should it do?

choices.text: Change the autoscaler to a lower target so that older VMs are replaced by autoscaling as load falls
Bake a patched image into a new instance template, then start a rolling update with surge and unavailable limits
Keep patching in place, but schedule it all at once on weekends so that every VM is at the same level
Delete the managed instance group, recreate it from the new template, and accept a short outage while it starts

stem: A retailer runs GKE Standard clusters and cannot tolerate node upgrades during the two-week holiday sales event, but it still wants security patches and version currency the rest of the year with little manual work. What configuration fits?

choices.text: Stay on a release channel, set a maintenance window for quiet hours, and add a maintenance exclusion for the event
Use a static version with no release channel and ignore upgrade notifications for the whole year
Disable auto-upgrade for the node pools permanently and upgrade them by hand whenever the team finds the time
Create a second cluster for the holiday period, and delete the first cluster after the event ends

stem: A bank deploys a GKE Standard private cluster whose nodes have no external IP addresses. Engineers reach the cluster only from the bank's corporate network, and the nodes must pull images from an external public registry and call a third-party SaaS API. Which TWO configurations fit? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Disabling the control plane's firewall so any client can use kubectl from the corporate network
External IP addresses on all nodes, so that image pulls and SaaS calls reach the internet directly
A Cloud NAT gateway for the cluster's subnet and Pod ranges, so that private nodes can make outbound internet connections
Private Google Access on the node subnet, to allow the nodes to reach the external registry and the SaaS API
Authorized networks on the control plane endpoint, limited to the corporate address ranges used by engineers

stem: An application's start-up takes about seven minutes, and its traffic follows a repeating daily and weekly pattern with a steep rise each morning. Reactive autoscaling on CPU lags behind the rise and users see slow responses until new instances are ready. Peak size varies from week to week, so fixed schedules would be wrong. What should the architect configure on the managed instance group?

choices.text: A zonal group instead of a regional group, since a single zone starts instances faster
A scheduled autoscaling rule that sets one fixed minimum number of instances for every weekday morning peak
A delay before each scale-out decision, so the autoscaler waits longer before adding more instances
Predictive autoscaling on the CPU-based autoscaler, plus an initialization period that matches the start-up time

stem: A software company must run a database product whose license is counted per physical core of the host server. Auditors require proof of how many physical cores and which servers the licensed VMs ran on. The company wants to use Compute Engine. Which option fits best?

choices.text: Sole-tenant nodes in a node group with node affinity, so licensed VMs run on dedicated hosts with visible usage
Shielded VMs with Confidential Computing, since hardware encryption lets the vendor verify the number of host cores
Spot VMs with a committed use discount, since cost reduction also reduces the number of cores the license counts
Standard multi-tenant VMs with the largest predefined machine type, since a larger VM always means fewer licensed cores

stem: A platform team runs stateless web services, nightly batch workers and a few stateful databases on one GKE Standard cluster. Cost must fall, but the databases and system components cannot tolerate abrupt node loss. How should it use Spot VMs?

choices.text: Convert every node pool to Spot VMs, since Kubernetes will reschedule any Pod elsewhere without risk or data loss
Run the whole cluster on standard nodes and use Spot VMs only for developer laptops outside GKE
Move the databases onto the Spot node pool, because GKE gives Spot nodes a long preemption warning
Add a separate Spot node pool and use a taint, toleration and node selector so only fault-tolerant Pods land there

stem: EHR Healthcare will store protected health information in Google Cloud and wants a technical guardrail so that engineers cannot use a Google Cloud service outside the ones covered by its Business Associate Agreement (BAA). Which approach best supports this goal?

choices.text: Pin all health data to a single region, because the BAA is valid only for services running in the region where the agreement was signed
Request a HIPAA certificate from the regulator for the Google Cloud project, since certification of the project is what makes every service in it acceptable
Accept the BAA, apply an organization policy limiting which services the health-data folder can use, and keep pre-GA offerings away from that data
Rely on the BAA alone, because it automatically blocks any service that is not covered, so engineers cannot reach an unsupported service by mistake

stem: EHR Healthcare needs consistent logging and retention across many projects. Auditors want admin and data-access records kept for seven years, and security staff in individual projects must not be able to shorten that period. An architect proposes a central design. Which design satisfies the requirement?

choices.text: Increase retention on the required log bucket in every project, so that all admin activity logs are held for seven years by default
Create an aggregated sink at the organization routing audit logs to a log bucket in a dedicated logging project, then set retention there and lock it
Leave each project on its default log bucket and ask project owners to raise the retention period when their team has a compliance need
Raise the retention period on the log buckets that exist at the organization level, because folder and organization buckets can be extended without limit

stem: A software company is preparing its own SOC 2 audit for a service that runs on Google Cloud. The auditor asks how Google Cloud's own attestations relate to the audit. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Because Google Cloud holds a SOC 2 report, every workload the company builds on it is automatically in scope and compliant without its own controls
The shared responsibility model shifts all application-level and configuration controls to Google, so the company only has to provide the invoice
Google Cloud's report replaces the need for the company to keep audit logs, because the provider retains all customer activity records for the auditor
Google Cloud publishes independent audit reports, such as SOC 2, that customers can download from the Compliance Reports Manager to evidence the provider's controls
The company must still document and operate its own controls, such as access reviews, change management and monitoring, for the parts of the stack it manages

stem: Cymbal Retail records calls from its IVR and call-center agents, who key in customer orders, and plans to send the transcripts to BigQuery for analytics and gen AI summaries. Callers read out payment card numbers, so the card data would spread into analytics datasets. What is the best design to keep card data out of those systems?

choices.text: Encrypt the transcript files with a customer-managed key and keep the card numbers in the text, so only key holders can read the content
Run the transcripts through Sensitive Data Protection to detect and redact card numbers before they are stored in the analytics datasets
Delete the transcripts after the analytics job finishes and leave the raw call recordings in the original bucket indefinitely
Store transcripts unchanged and rely on the BigQuery dataset permissions to keep analysts from reading the card numbers in the text

stem: A retailer must demonstrate PCI DSS compliance for its checkout application. A developer says that because Google Cloud's services are certified for PCI DSS, the application is automatically compliant. Which response, and the design choice that follows from it, is most accurate?

choices.text: The services give a compliant base, but the application and its configuration must be assessed; isolating checkout in its own project and network narrows scope
The developer is right as long as the application uses only managed services, since managed services remove every customer responsibility under the standard
Compliance is impossible on shared infrastructure, so the retailer must move checkout to dedicated hardware outside Google Cloud
The developer is right, because the assessor's report on the underlying services is accepted as the retailer's own validation for any workload running there

stem: A language-learning company is launching a mobile app for children under 13 and runs it on Google Cloud. The legal team cites the U.S. children's privacy law (COPPA). Which architectural approach best supports the privacy obligations without claiming that the platform alone makes the company compliant?

choices.text: Store child data in the same wide analytics tables as adult users and tag the rows, because separate storage makes deletion requests harder to run
Rely on Google Cloud's compliance page to state that COPPA is satisfied for all customers, so no design work on data handling is required
Collect only the data the app needs, keep child data in a dedicated, access-limited dataset with expiry, and be able to find and delete one child's records
Collect as much usage data as possible now and decide later which records the team is allowed to keep, because large datasets are easier to anonymize afterward

stem: KnightMotives must comply with EU data protection rules. Its legal team requires that EU customer data stay in EU locations and that Google support personnel who could access the data be located in the EU. An engineer proposes only an organization policy that restricts resource locations to EU regions. Why is that proposal incomplete, and what fits better?

choices.text: The proposal is incomplete because the location constraint cannot cover storage, so the team should instead use a VPN to keep traffic inside the EU
The location constraint also controls which Google personnel can access the data, so the proposal is complete and Assured Workloads adds nothing for residency needs
The location constraint only works for multi-region locations, so the team must use a single-region bucket and enable Data Access audit logs
Residency policy limits where resources are created but not who supports them; an Assured Workloads EU Data Boundary and Support package adds personnel controls

stem: A German health insurer's regulator requires that customer data stay in Germany. An analytics team created a BigQuery dataset in the EU multi-region, and reviewers say this may not meet the rule. The team asks what to change. Which is the correct resolution?

choices.text: Create a new dataset in a single region in Germany, copy the tables into it, and add an organization policy that blocks creating datasets outside allowed locations
Keep the EU multi-region dataset and enable CMEK on it, because customer-managed keys make the data physically stay inside one country
Keep the dataset and configure a query reservation in Germany, because the reservation location decides where the stored tables live
Edit the existing dataset and switch its location to a German region, because a dataset's location can be changed at any time without recreating or copying anything

stem: A public-sector customer's compliance team requires that Google personnel can reach its content only after the customer's own administrator has approved the request, and that the customer can later review a log of what Google personnel did. Which TWO controls together meet this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: An IAM deny policy on the support roles at the organization, because Google employees are principals in the customer's own allow policies
A VPC Service Controls perimeter around the projects, because Google employees are outside the perimeter and cannot cross it for support
Access Approval, so that an authorized administrator in the customer's organization must approve each request before a Google administrator gets access
Data Access audit logs on every service, because they record the actions of Google support staff inside the customer's projects as well
Access Transparency logs, which give the customer a view of actions by Google authorized personnel for support requests and service availability

stem: A hospital group wants to share FHIR patient records stored in the Cloud Healthcare API with an external research team. The researchers should not receive direct identifiers, but the hospital wants the originals to stay intact. What is the most appropriate approach?

choices.text: Export the original FHIR resources to a Cloud Storage bucket and remove the identifiers manually in a spreadsheet before sharing
Use the Cloud Healthcare API de-identification to create a de-identified copy of the FHIR data in a separate dataset, and share only that copy
Delete the identifying fields in the original FHIR store, since a sharing copy is not required once the originals are edited in place
Give the research team read access to the original FHIR store and ask them in the contract to ignore identifiers in the records

stem: A hospital research team will release a de-identified table of patient visits to external researchers. Names are already removed, but ZIP code, birth year and sex remain. The privacy officer wants to measure how easily individuals could still be singled out through combinations of these columns before release. Which Sensitive Data Protection capability fits?

choices.text: Date shifting on the birth year column, because shifting guarantees that no two rows can ever be matched to the same person
A deterministic tokenization pass on every column, because tokens make a table equally safe regardless of which columns remain
Re-identification risk analysis with a k-anonymity metric, using ZIP code, birth year and sex as the quasi-identifiers
An inspection job with built-in infoTypes, because counting name and card number matches also measures how unique each row is

stem: A health research team trains a model on patient visit records that contain exact ages and visit dates. The privacy officer wants to reduce re-identification risk while keeping the data useful: the order and spacing of each patient's visits must be preserved. Which TWO Sensitive Data Protection transformations fit this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Date shifting, which moves dates by a random amount, consistent per patient, so the order and intervals between visits stay intact
Replacement of every date with the same fixed value, which preserves the order of visits for each patient
Cryptographic hashing of the dates, which keeps the intervals between visits available for analysis and for the model
Redaction of all the date columns, which still keeps the sequence of visits available to the model during training
Bucketing, which replaces exact ages with age ranges so that individual patients are harder to single out

stem: KnightMotives requires that all log data of its EU projects stays in the EU. A reviewer finds that the `_Required` and `_Default` log buckets of new projects are stored in the global location. What should the architect do?

choices.text: Edit the location of each existing `_Default` bucket to an EU region, because log bucket locations can be changed whenever the data needs to move
Set default resource settings for Cloud Logging on the organization with an EU storage location, so new projects create their `_Required` and `_Default` buckets there
Enable CMEK with an EU key on the global buckets, because the key location decides in which country the encrypted log entries are stored
Route all logs with a sink to a user-defined EU bucket and consider the matter closed, because the `_Required` bucket then holds no log entries at all

stem: A financial firm must keep audit records for seven years in a form that nobody, including project owners, can edit or remove early, and must be able to prove this to regulators. Logs are produced by many projects. Which design best fits?

choices.text: Export the logs into a BigQuery dataset and give project owners the BigQuery Data Editor role so they can correct bad records
Keep the logs in each project's default log bucket and set a seven-year retention using a scheduled reminder to the project owners
Route the logs to a Cloud Storage bucket with a retention policy but leave it unlocked, so the administrators can adjust it if needed
Route the logs with a sink to a Cloud Storage bucket that has a retention policy of seven years and lock that policy

stem: A public-sector customer built an Assured Workloads folder for a regulated data boundary. A developer wants to use a newly released Google Cloud service that is not shown in the list of supported products for that control package. What is the best guidance?

choices.text: Use it after moving it to a project outside the folder, because the control package then applies the folder's controls to the project retroactively
Keep it away from regulated data until it is listed for the package, because unsupported services have not met all controls; block it with an organization policy
Use it if its API endpoint is shared with a supported product, because a shared endpoint means the service has been authorized for the package
Use it freely, because everything created in an Assured Workloads folder is automatically covered by the control package, whatever the service involved

stem: A company has an organization policy that restricts resource creation to EU locations. Its compliance officer also wants to know quickly if someone creates a resource that drifts from the compliance posture in ways the policy does not prevent, such as a misconfigured storage bucket. Which combination describes preventive versus detective controls correctly?

choices.text: The location policy is preventive, as it blocks creation outside allowed places; Security Command Center posture and compliance findings are detective
Both are preventive, because every control in Google Cloud blocks non-compliant configurations before they are applied to a resource
Both are detective, because organization policies only create findings that an administrator reads after the resource already exists
The location policy is detective, because it reports on resources created outside the EU, and Security Command Center is preventive because it denies the API calls

stem: KnightMotives stores driver profiles in the EU and must support deletion requests under EU data protection rules. Profile data is copied into backups, analytics tables and training sets, which makes locating every copy hard. Which design best makes deletion practical?

choices.text: Keep profile data forever in one large unpartitioned table and tell customers that deletion requests can only be answered after about five years
Share one customer-managed key across all profiles, because destroying that key on request deletes only that one person's data and no one else's
Copy the data to every region for resilience first, because having more copies of each profile makes a deletion request easier to complete
Encrypt each person's data with its own Cloud KMS key, so destroying a key makes every copy unreadable, and keep an index of where data is stored
