stem: A car maker stores EU driver telemetry in a BigQuery dataset located in the EU. Analysts in the United States need monthly trends from it. The company wants to maintain EU residency of the personal data. Which approach is best?

choices.text: Copy the raw telemetry into a US dataset, since analysts get faster queries and simpler permissions when the data is in their own region
Set up a US project that reads the EU tables and caches the raw rows in its own storage, refreshing them whenever the analysts ask
Let analysts query the EU dataset, where processing happens, and give them only aggregated or de-identified result tables rather than raw copies
Export the raw data to a US Cloud Storage bucket every night and load it into a US dataset, where the analysts can work with it

stem: A SaaS vendor hosts regulated customer data for hundreds of tenants on Google Cloud. Contracts say the customer owns the data, and when a contract ends the vendor must return it and be able to prove it can no longer read it. Which design best supports this?

choices.text: Mix all tenants into shared tables with a tenant column, and delete that tenant's rows by query when a contract ends, without any further proof
Use one shared key for the whole platform, and revoke the vendor's own access at termination to show that the data is no longer being used
Store tenant data under the vendor's personal accounts, so the vendor can hand over the entire account to the customer when the contract ends
Give each tenant its own project and Cloud KMS key, so data can be exported per tenant and the key destroyed at termination to make copies unreadable

stem: KnightMotives, an EU car maker, will process driver personal data on Google Cloud. Its legal team asks how the GDPR roles and contract fit together. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: Signing up for Google Cloud makes Google the controller of the drivers' data, so the car maker has no GDPR duties left for the data held there
The customer acts as controller and Google as processor under the Google Cloud data processing terms, which commit Google to process data per the customer's instructions
Google's GDPR page certifies the car maker's applications, so no assessment of its own processing purposes or legal basis is needed
Data processing terms are optional for GDPR, because the regulation applies only to the provider and never to customers of cloud services

stem: Altostrat Media's build pipeline must pull internal libraries from an artifact server that is reachable only on a private network connected to Google Cloud, while the builds themselves should stay fully managed. Which Cloud Build option fits?

choices.text: A private pool that peers into the VPC network, so build steps can reach private resources
The default pool with the artifact server's address published on the public internet for the build workers
The default pool, because its workers have a route into every customer VPC network by default
A self-managed build server on a long-running VM, because Cloud Build cannot reach private resources in any form

stem: A team ships container images to production several times a day. A security lead wants known vulnerabilities in dependencies detected early, as part of the software development lifecycle, rather than found in production. Which approach best shifts this check left?

choices.text: Ask developers to read public vulnerability lists every week and manually compare them with the dependencies that each service uses
Scan only the base image on the developer's laptop and skip registry scanning, because the final image is rebuilt again later in the pipeline
Turn on automatic scanning in Artifact Registry so every pushed image is scanned, and stop promotion in the pipeline when serious findings appear
Run a vulnerability scan once a year on the production cluster, and accept the findings at the next planned maintenance window of the team

stem: A development team wants each pull request tested against a realistic copy of the production architecture, including a database and a load balancer, without maintaining a permanent test environment that is mostly idle. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: Test directly in production behind a feature flag, because no separate environment can ever be accurate enough to be useful
Keep one shared test environment permanently running, and ask developers to take turns using it whenever they need to test a change
Run the tests only on developers' laptops, because production-like environments cannot be created automatically for a pull request
Define the stack as code with Terraform, create it per pull request in the pipeline, run the tests, then destroy it

stem: EHR Healthcare suffered past outages caused by misconfiguration. After a new incident, customer-facing latency began to rise at 02:10 and a service stopped answering at 02:25. The team suspects that a change was made shortly before. What is the most direct way to test that hypothesis as part of root cause analysis?

choices.text: Check the Data Access audit logs of the database for reads, because reads always explain why a service becomes slow
Query the Admin Activity audit logs for configuration and IAM changes made shortly before 02:10 and compare them with the metrics timeline
Restart every service in the affected project, then record whether the latency drops and call the restart the root cause
Ask each engineer whether they remember changing anything, and close the analysis if nobody recalls a change at that time

stem: A microservices application on GKE shows a rise in 99th percentile latency for checkout requests. Average latency looks normal. Which TWO actions most directly lead to the root cause? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Compare the monthly bill for the project, since a cost change identifies the failing dependency
Turn off the instrumentation to remove overhead, then watch whether the p99 drops
Open the log entries linked to the slow traces through the trace ID to see errors, retries or timeouts in that exact request
Raise the node count in the cluster, because more nodes reliably remove a latency spike for every kind of cause
Use Cloud Trace to view the spans of slow requests and find which downstream call or service contributes most of the time

stem: Altostrat Media's teams deploy containers to GKE clusters by running scripts from their laptops. The platform lead wants central management of releases: the same release moves from staging to production in a defined order, production needs an explicit approval, and audit details are kept. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Define a Cloud Deploy delivery pipeline with staging and production targets, set the production target to require approval, and promote the release through them
Trigger a Cloud Build job that deploys to production automatically on every merge, so that no step waits for a person and approval is unnecessary
Keep the laptop scripts and add a shared document where engineers write which cluster each release was deployed to and who approved it
Give each team its own copy of the pipeline definition with a different promotion order, so that every team can choose the checks that suit it

stem: Minutes after a release to production, Error Reporting shows a new error group that appears only for the new version, and users are seeing failures. What is the best order of actions?

choices.text: Add more instances of the new version, because errors that appear right after a release are caused by too little capacity
Mitigate first by rolling back or shifting traffic from the new version, then use the stack traces and logs of the error group to find the cause
Keep the new version serving traffic until the full root cause is found, since rolling back would destroy the evidence for analysis
Delete the error group in Error Reporting so the dashboard looks clean, then wait for further user reports to arrive

stem: A team builds a container image in development and then rebuilds it from source for staging and again for production. Occasionally production behaves differently from the tested staging build. Which TWO practices fix this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Rebuild the image in production with the latest dependency versions, so production always has the newest libraries
Tag images with a moving label such as latest, so each environment pulls whatever was published last
Build the image once in CI, store it in Artifact Registry, and promote the same image, referenced by its digest, through staging to production
Bake the production database address into the image, so no configuration is needed at deployment
Keep environment-specific settings, such as endpoints and credentials references, outside the image and inject them at deployment

stem: EHR Healthcare keeps legacy insurer interfaces on premises, linked to Google Cloud over a private connection. After a new claims service is deployed, the insurer's on-premises server cannot reach it, and network and platform teams each say their side is fine. Which first step most quickly shows where the packet path breaks?

choices.text: Enable Packet Mirroring on every subnet in the project and review the captured traffic once the next insurer attempt arrives
Open a firewall rule that allows all ingress from any address to the claims service so the cause can be ruled out by trial and error
Delete and recreate the private connection to the on-premises data center, hoping that a reset restores whatever routes are missing
Run Connectivity Tests from the on-premises source address to the claims service and read which route or firewall rule stops the path

stem: A team puts a new external Application Load Balancer in front of a managed instance group. Opening a VM's service port from inside the VPC returns the right page, yet every backend is reported unhealthy and users receive error responses. The instances were created in a VPC that has no custom firewall rules yet. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: No ingress allow rule permits the Google Cloud health check probe ranges, so the implied deny rule blocks the probes
The instance group was created as zonal, and zonal groups cannot receive health check probes from the load balancer
The health check must use the same protocol as client traffic, so a TCP check cannot be used with an HTTPS frontend
The load balancer needs a static external IP address attached to each instance before health checks can succeed

stem: Batch worker VMs in a private subnet have no external IP addresses. Security policy forbids any route from them to the public internet. After a new subnet is created, jobs that read from Cloud Storage and call Google APIs time out, while the same code worked in the older subnet. What should the architect check and fix first?

choices.text: Add a Cloud NAT gateway for the subnet so workers can reach the storage endpoint over the public internet
Move the workers to the default network where Google APIs are reachable without a subnet setting
Check that Private Google Access is on for the new subnet, since VMs without external IPs need it to reach Google APIs
Attach an external IP to each worker VM, then limit outbound traffic with firewall rules so that only the storage service is allowed

stem: After a marketing event, a GKE Standard cluster with node autoscaling enabled leaves new Pods in Pending state for hours, although the node pool maximum is far above the current node count. Which TWO actions most directly reveal the root cause? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Disable the autoscaler and add nodes by hand, then see whether the Pods start without further investigation
Read the cluster autoscaler visibility events in Cloud Logging, especially noScaleUp entries, which state why scale-up was blocked
Delete the Pending Pods and recreate the Deployments, since stuck scheduling state is usually cleared by this
Double the CPU requests on all Deployments so the scheduler places the Pods on the nodes that already exist
Check project quotas for the machine type and the free IP addresses left in the Pod range of the subnet

stem: A platform team stores Terraform for production networks and databases in Git. After an incident caused by a misconfigured public database, the CISO wants infrastructure changes tested and validated before they reach production. Which TWO controls best provide this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Review the changed Terraform files by eye during a monthly meeting and apply them in bulk after the meeting
Run every change in a developer project with relaxed organization policies so errors surface where they cost little
Apply changes straight to production and rely on Cloud Audit Logs afterwards to show whether anything unsafe was created by the change
Preview each deployment to see what resources will change, and require approval of that preview before the pipeline applies it
Evaluate the plan of each pull request against policy-as-code rules, such as no public database addresses, before a merge is allowed

stem: KnightMotives wants regional sales managers, who are not engineers and must hold no infrastructure permissions, to request a standard dealer-portal environment on demand. Today every request is a ticket that waits days for the platform team. Which design gives self-service without handing out broad rights?

choices.text: A request form that starts a pipeline applying an approved, versioned Terraform blueprint through a dedicated service account that holds only the roles it needs
Grant each sales manager the Editor role on a shared sandbox project and share a written checklist for building the environment in the console
Give every sales manager the Owner role on the dealer-portal project so that each can run the deployment tool directly and change settings as needed
Email the platform team a copy of the template with edited values for each request, so that an engineer applies it by hand from a laptop

stem: A growing company opens a new Google Cloud project for every new product team by raising a ticket. The central cloud team needs several days per ticket, and projects come out with inconsistent labels, budgets and API settings. The company wants speed without losing control. Which approach is best?

choices.text: Keep the manual ticket process but hire more people for the cloud team to shorten the time per request
Allow all engineers to create projects anywhere in the organization and ask them to follow a naming guideline and add labels when they remember
Move every team into one shared project so that no new projects need to be created at all
Automate creation with a Terraform project factory that sets folder, billing link, labels, budget and enabled APIs

stem: Batch workers in a private subnet, with no external IP addresses, reach a partner's API through a Cloud NAT gateway. Each night, when many workers start at once, some calls fail with connection errors, while the same calls succeed during the day. Which action most directly finds the cause?

choices.text: Open the partner's address range in an egress firewall rule, because nightly failures are normally caused by a missing allow rule
Read the Cloud NAT gateway logs and metrics for dropped connections, then compare the ports per VM with the simultaneous connections
Increase the machine type of the batch workers so that each VM can open more outbound connections to the partner at the same time
Replace the private subnet with one that gives every worker an external IP address, so that no translation limit can apply to them

stem: A company has written disaster recovery runbooks for its order system, backed by replication to a second region. It has never failed over. Which practice best confirms that the plan will really meet the recovery objectives?

choices.text: Review the written plan and runbooks with senior management in a yearly meeting and have them sign it off as the approved plan
Restore backups into an isolated environment each quarter and count the test as passed whenever the restore job reports that it has finished
Schedule failover exercises that bring up the order system in the second region, with the people who would operate it, and measure the achieved recovery time and data loss
Keep a dashboard of replication job status in the monitoring tool and treat a continuous healthy status as proof that recovery will succeed

stem: Altostrat Media still runs its content ingestion system in one on-premises data center. A disaster there could be tolerated for up to four hours, and the budget is limited. The business wants a recovery site in Google Cloud. Which design fits best?

choices.text: Pilot light: replicate ingestion data to Google Cloud continuously, keep the infrastructure as code, and start compute only after a disaster is declared
Active-active across two on-premises sites, which removes the dependency on Google Cloud entirely
Hot standby: run a full-size copy of the ingestion system in Google Cloud at all times, send half of live traffic to it, and keep it patched in step
Cold backup: copy files to Cloud Storage monthly and build the whole environment manually from documents after a disaster

stem: A software vendor runs stateful applications with persistent volumes on a regional GKE cluster. To prepare for the loss of an entire region, the team needs to restore Kubernetes resources and persistent data into a cluster elsewhere. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Rely on the regional cluster's multiple zones, since zones in the same region protect against a regional outage
Use Backup for GKE with scheduled plans that capture configuration and volume snapshots, then restore into a cluster in another region
Back up only the container images in Artifact Registry, since images contain all of the application state
Take a snapshot of the control plane datastore and import it into a new cluster in another region, because GKE exposes it for this purpose

stem: A hospital group's patient portal on Cloud Run often returns errors during traffic spikes. Logs show the Cloud SQL for MySQL database rejecting new connections with "too many connections", although CPU and memory on the database stay low. What is the most likely root cause and fix?

choices.text: The database has too little storage, so increasing disk size will release the connection slots currently in use
Cloud Run is the wrong platform for databases, so the portal must move back to virtual machines, which have no connection limit at all
Read traffic is too high, so adding a cross-region replica will let write requests succeed
Each scaled-out instance opens its own connections: cap them per instance, use pooling, and limit maximum instances to what the database can serve

stem: Cymbal Retail has piloted generative AI that creates product attributes and descriptions from supplier data, and wants to expand to all verticals. Before expansion the architect must define how the output is tested and validated. Which approach is best?

choices.text: Build a labeled evaluation set per vertical from known-good entries, set acceptance thresholds, and keep human review before catalog updates
Have the merchandising lead read about ten generated items and approve the expansion if they look good
Ask the model to rate its own outputs and approve any item with a high self-score
Publish generated content directly to the live catalog and watch conversion and return rates after launch to find the content that is wrong

stem: In a design review for a new customer data platform, the security lead insists on private-only access and a lengthy approval flow, while the product owner demands a launch in six weeks for a customer commitment. The two cannot agree. What should the architect do?

choices.text: Side with the product owner, because revenue commitments outweigh internal controls, and fix security gaps after launch
Ask the two to settle it between themselves and attend later only if they ask for a ruling
Clarify each side's underlying requirement, present options with risk, cost and timing, and bring the choice to the accountable executive
Tell the product owner the launch must slip until every security preference is met, because the architect has no right to weigh them against dates

stem: A company designs a migration of its payment systems. Two weeks before cutover, the compliance team announces it must approve data location and audit logging, which the design does not address. Which practice would most likely have prevented this?

choices.text: Sending a weekly email to the whole company with the migration schedule so nobody can claim they were unaware
Adding a compliance review at the very end of the project, after the design and the implementation are finished and tested by the team
Do a stakeholder analysis at the start, listing every affected group and involving each in design reviews by its interest and influence
Letting the engineering team collect requirements alone, because other groups do not understand the technology and would only slow the design down

stem: KnightMotives is rolling out a new CRM and sales tool to its dealers, who have no equipment budget and mixed digital skills. A previous online ordering system was forced on dealers and was unreliable, so trust is low. Which change management approach is most likely to succeed?

choices.text: Postpone the rollout until the in-vehicle experience program finishes, so dealers are not asked to change twice
Pilot with a few willing dealers, act on their feedback, offer training and support, then expand in waves with a tool that needs no new hardware
Mandate the tool in a memo and track adoption in usage reports, with penalties for dealers who fall behind the schedule
Switch all dealers on the same weekend and cancel the old tools immediately, to avoid supporting two systems

stem: A company's weekly change advisory board approves every production change, including small automated deployments. Deployments queue for days, and developers bypass the process during emergencies. The company wants faster delivery without losing control. What should the architect recommend?

choices.text: Require two board members to approve each change instead of one, since stricter review of every change reduces the temptation to bypass it
Remove approvals completely and let developers deploy any change when they decide it is ready
Keep the board unchanged but move its meeting to daily so that the queue is shorter
Pre-approve low-risk standard changes behind automated pipeline gates, and keep the board for high-risk or novel changes

stem: EHR Healthcare's operations team knows virtual machines and Microsoft Active Directory well, but has never run Kubernetes at scale. Within a year it must operate several container environments on Google Cloud. What is the best plan for team readiness?

choices.text: Assess skills against the target operating model, then provide training paths, sandbox practice and partner support during early production
Hire a few Kubernetes experts and leave the existing team on the legacy VM systems for the remaining years
Send the team a list of documentation links and expect it to learn on the job, mostly during the first real production incident of the year
Defer all container work until every team member holds a Kubernetes certification, even if the lease deadline passes

stem: A four-person team with no container experience must run a stateless HTTP API that has variable traffic and no special networking needs. The platform decision is due this week. Which choice best reflects the team's skills and the requirements?

choices.text: Several Compute Engine VMs behind a load balancer, with software installed by hand, because virtual machines are familiar to every administrator
Cloud Run, where the team deploys a container and the platform handles scaling and infrastructure, with a later move to GKE if requirements grow
A GKE Standard cluster with custom node pools, so the team keeps full control of the nodes
A self-managed Kubernetes cluster on Compute Engine, because it is the most portable platform and the team can learn it during the project

stem: Two years after a design decision to use a regional GKE cluster with a specific database, new team members keep reopening the discussion because nobody remembers why the choices were made. What practice best addresses this decision-making problem?

choices.text: Record architecture decisions in architecture decision records stored near the code, capturing context, options considered, the decision and the reasons
Store only the final diagrams and configuration files, because the reasons for each choice are visible in the architecture that results from them
Keep the reasoning in the memory of the original architect, who joins the next meeting when asked
Make every decision a company-wide vote so that there is no later need to explain it

stem: An architecture team has spent three weeks debating which dashboard tool to adopt, while the question of which regions will hold regulated customer data has not been examined. Which approach improves the team's decision making?

choices.text: Settle both topics with a vote today, because moving quickly is the main objective of a decision process
Postpone both until the next annual planning cycle so that all stakeholders can consider them together
Give both topics identical, extensive analysis, because a consistent process matters more than the effect that each decision has on the business
Settle the dashboard tool with a short time-boxed trial, as it is easy to reverse, and analyze the costly region decision rigorously

stem: A data team lead wants Spanner for a new transactional service; the application team prefers Cloud SQL for familiarity. Both argue from experience, and no measured data exists on the real workload's scale or latency. How should the architect move the decision forward?

choices.text: Choose the option that more senior people support, since experience is the best predictor of success
Pick the cheaper option by list price without any testing, and revisit the choice if the service has problems after it has launched
Run a time-boxed proof of concept on the real access patterns with agreed success criteria and cost estimates, then decide from the results
Pick Spanner because it is the more scalable product, which is always the safer choice for new services

stem: A bank introduces a virtual agent that handles routine questions. Call-center employees fear that the project will make their jobs redundant, and some have started to criticize it publicly. Which TWO actions best address this change management risk? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Tell employees that the assistant is optional and will not be used, then expand it quietly later
Keep the project plan confidential until launch day, so that rumors have less time to spread
Involve experienced agents in designing and testing the assistant, and explain how roles will shift toward complex cases, with reskilling support
Replace the critical employees' work with the assistant first, since they are the most resistant and the loudest voices in the team
Communicate honestly and regularly about goals, scope and timeline, and publish adoption and quality results from the pilot

stem: A cloud program has stakeholders from finance, security, operations, application teams and an executive sponsor. Status reports so far were one long technical document, and finance and the sponsor say they do not read them. Which TWO actions improve stakeholder management? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Limit communication to the weekly engineering meeting, because the decisions that matter to the program are made by engineers anyway
Send the same long report to everyone more often, so that each reader can find what they need
Share only good news with the sponsor to keep confidence in the program high
Agree with each stakeholder group what it needs to know and decide, and tailor the content and cadence, such as spend and risk summaries for finance and the sponsor
Define success criteria and decision rights with the stakeholders at the start, and report progress against them, including risks and open decisions

stem: A company has adopted a new CI/CD pipeline and wants all fifteen development teams to use it within six months. An earlier attempt to introduce a build tool was ignored by most teams. Which TWO actions best support adoption? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Tie each developer's yearly rating to the number of pipeline runs, so that usage rises quickly
Name respected engineers in a few teams as champions, who help colleagues, collect feedback and demonstrate benefits
Keep training optional and available only as documentation, so that teams can choose their own pace
Announce a single cutover date after which the old pipelines are disabled for every team, with no trial or fallback period before it
Onboard teams in waves, starting with teams that have simple needs, track adoption and deployment metrics, and fix pipeline issues between waves

stem: EHR Healthcare keeps scanned claim attachments for many medical-office tenants in one Cloud Storage bucket, under one prefix per tenant. Each tenant's service account must read and write only its own prefix. The platform team wants to manage this without touching individual objects, and wants no legacy object ACL to be able to grant surprise access. Which configuration fits?

choices.text: Turn on uniform bucket-level access, create a managed folder per tenant prefix and grant each tenant's service account Storage Object User on it
Grant all tenant service accounts Storage Object Viewer on the project and filter by tenant prefix in the shared application code that serves them
Keep fine-grained access on the bucket and set an object ACL naming the tenant's service account on every attachment as the upload job writes it
Create one bucket per tenant and grant each tenant's service account Storage Admin on the project so that it can manage its own bucket

stem: Cymbal Retail's suppliers overwrite their catalog feed file in Cloud Storage several times a day. Object Versioning is enabled so that a bad feed can be rolled back, but noncurrent versions have piled up and storage cost keeps growing. Rollback is only ever needed within 30 days, and the current (live) feed objects must never be removed automatically. Which change fits?

choices.text: Add a lifecycle rule with the Delete action and a condition on days since the version became noncurrent set to 30
Add a lifecycle rule that moves every noncurrent version to Archive storage so that the stored bytes become cheaper
Add a lifecycle rule with the Delete action and an age condition of 30 days, applied to all objects in the bucket
Disable Object Versioning on the bucket so that overwritten feeds no longer create noncurrent versions

stem: A health insurer must keep adjudicated claim records unaltered for seven years. Auditors require evidence that no one, including project owners, can delete or replace a record before it is seven years old or shorten that period. Which design satisfies the requirement?

choices.text: A lifecycle rule that never deletes claim records, combined with a restricted set of administrators
A seven-year bucket retention policy locked with Bucket Lock, tried first on a test bucket
Object Versioning on the bucket plus an IAM deny policy so that no principal can delete noncurrent versions or change the bucket settings
A bucket with soft delete retention raised to the maximum duration, so that any deleted or overwritten claim record can be restored by the team

stem: A software vendor's licensed database must stay on Compute Engine VMs. It holds about 500 GB, but peak load needs far more IOPS than the team's current SSD Persistent Disk delivers at that size, and the demand changes through the year. The team wants to raise or lower performance while the VM runs without paying for capacity it does not need. Which storage choice fits?

choices.text: Switch to standard Persistent Disk and raise the vCPU count of the VM so that it can issue more requests
Enlarge the SSD Persistent Disk to several terabytes so that it inherits the higher IOPS limits that come with size
Move the data files to Local SSD attached to the VM, which has the lowest latency of all block options
Use a Hyperdisk Balanced volume with IOPS and throughput provisioned separately from its size and adjusted in use

stem: A machine-learning team trains models on accelerators in a single zone. Checkpoints and training shards are read and written constantly, and object latency from a regular bucket leaves the accelerators idle. The team still wants Cloud Storage semantics and lowest latency, close to the VMs. Which TWO configuration decisions apply? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Create a dual-region bucket with turbo replication so that a copy of the data sits near the VMs
Enable Autoclass on a regional bucket so that hot checkpoints are promoted to the Rapid storage class
Create a zonal bucket in the same zone as the accelerator VMs, which uses the Rapid storage class
Set the default storage class of a regional bucket to Nearline so that reads are served from a cache
Enable hierarchical namespace and uniform bucket-level access, which Rapid Bucket requires

stem: A healthcare software vendor runs SQL Server and MySQL on Compute Engine VMs while it migrates. Leadership fears a ransomware attack in which stolen administrator credentials are used to delete backups. Which TWO design points best address this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Send backups to a Backup and DR backup vault that enforces a minimum retention period and is immutable and indelible
Export database dumps to a Standard bucket in the same project, with Object Versioning enabled and a lifecycle rule that keeps 30 days
Take disk snapshots in the same project as the VMs and rely on a small Owner group to prevent deletions
Attach a second persistent disk to each VM and copy the data nightly with a cron job
Define a backup plan with backup rules that set the frequency and retention for the VMs, using application-consistent backups

stem: A publisher's organization enforces public access prevention on all projects. A partner without any Google account must download one finished episode file for the next 48 hours, and the publisher does not want to copy the file elsewhere or make the bucket public. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Make the object public with allUsers read access for 48 hours and then remove the grant
Generate a V4 signed URL for the object with a 48-hour expiry, using a service account that can read the object
Create Google accounts for the partner's staff and grant Storage Object Viewer on the project containing the bucket
Grant allAuthenticatedUsers the Storage Object Viewer role on the object so that any person with a Google account can read it

stem: A team enabled Object Versioning on forty buckets only to recover from accidental or malicious deletions and overwrites. Nobody ever restores a specific older version, but storage cost has grown because every overwrite keeps a full copy. The team wants time-bounded recovery of deleted or overwritten objects without a growing pile of versions. What should the architect recommend?

choices.text: Apply a locked retention policy to every bucket so that no object can be deleted or overwritten for the whole retention period
Enable Autoclass on all buckets so that older copies are cheaper to keep
Rely on soft delete with a longer retention duration for these buckets, and keep versioning only where specific older versions are needed
Keep versioning and add a lifecycle rule to move all noncurrent versions to Coldline

stem: A team schedules a nightly retraining pipeline on Agent Platform Pipelines. The ingest step reads a BigQuery table through a query string that never changes, and the run finishes in minutes but the model never reflects new rows. The team still wants costly feature-engineering steps to be skipped when their inputs are unchanged. What is the best fix?

choices.text: Increase the machine type of the training step so that it picks up the newest rows in the table
Rewrite the pipeline with the TFX SDK instead of Kubeflow Pipelines so that ingest steps are rerun automatically each night
Turn off caching for the entire pipeline job on every run, so that every step recomputes each night
Pass the run date to the ingest step as an input parameter, or turn off caching for that task only, and keep caching on for the other steps

stem: Altostrat Media requires its recommendation models to be auditable and explainable. For any model in production, reviewers must be able to show which datasets, parameters and pipeline run produced it. Training is currently run from individual notebooks. Which approach best meets this?

choices.text: Write the training scripts to Cloud Logging and search the logs when auditors ask for the history of a model
Store the training code in Git with tagged releases, relying on commit history as the record of what produced each model
Run training as Agent Platform Pipelines tasks so ML Metadata records lineage, and register each model in Model Registry
Keep training in notebooks and record the dataset names and parameters in a shared team spreadsheet

stem: An insurer's analytics team stores customer features in BigQuery. A fraud model must fetch the latest features for one customer at low latency during online prediction, and the team wants to avoid building and maintaining a second copy of the feature data. Which design fits?

choices.text: Copy the features nightly into a self-managed Bigtable instance with a custom ETL job and read from it
Query BigQuery directly from the prediction service for every request, using a standard on-demand query on the feature table
Cache the entire feature table in Memorystore and rebuild the cache whenever a feature value changes
Use Agent Platform Feature Store with the BigQuery tables as the data source and serve features online through it

stem: A pipeline's preprocessing task currently loads 8 TB of clickstream data into one container, joins it with warehouse tables in memory and often runs out of memory. The team wants the pipeline to stay the single orchestrator of the ML workflow. What should the architect recommend?

choices.text: Split the preprocessing into many identical containers that each load all 8 TB and write partial results
Have tasks submit the SQL joins to BigQuery and the large-scale parsing to Dataflow, then pass the outputs on
Run the preprocessing task on the largest machine type available and keep the in-memory join in the container
Drop the pipeline and ask analysts to run preprocessing by hand in notebooks before each training run

stem: A research group is picking accelerators for two training workloads. Which TWO workloads are the best candidates for Cloud TPUs? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A model dominated by large matrix multiplications, trained with large batches and scaled across many chips
A model with many custom PyTorch operations in the main loop that run partly on CPUs
A model with a large number of custom TensorFlow operations written in C++ that must run on the host CPU
A model that uses TensorFlow operations that are not available on Cloud TPU
A large transformer written in JAX whose training loop is dominated by dense matrix computations, with no custom operations in the main loop

stem: A team fine-tunes a model on an 8-GPU VM for two to three days per run. The job has no checkpointing, so a preemption would lose all progress. The job may wait several hours for capacity to start, and the team wants a discount compared with on-demand without buying a reservation. Which consumption option fits?

choices.text: Flex-start, which waits for capacity, runs for up to seven days and is not preemptible
Standard on-demand VMs, requested again on a loop until the capacity is available
Spot VMs, which give the deepest discount and are started immediately based on availability
A future reservation in advance, with a commitment, even though the job runs only now and then

stem: KnightMotives trains perception models on hundreds of terabytes of sensor recordings kept in Cloud Storage. The training code on a GKE cluster of GPU nodes expects shared POSIX paths, and the GPUs sit mostly idle while waiting for data. Which storage design best fixes the bottleneck?

choices.text: Keep reading from a regional Cloud Storage bucket, but add more GPU nodes to the cluster to hide the waiting time
Put the data in a dual-region bucket with turbo replication to speed up reads from the cluster
Mount a Managed Lustre file system on the nodes and import the training data from Cloud Storage into it
Create a Filestore instance in a basic tier and copy the recordings from the bucket for each experiment

stem: Altostrat Media wants to detect harmful content in its stored video library. The team wants a prebuilt API that analyzes the video files and flags explicit scenes with timestamps, without training a model or writing prompts. Which service fits?

choices.text: Cloud Natural Language API on the transcripts of the videos
Video Intelligence API with the explicit content detection feature
Cloud Speech-to-Text on the audio tracks of the videos
Cloud Vision API, called on each exported still frame of the videos

stem: Cymbal Retail wants to produce image variations and masked edits (for example, a new background) from supplier product photos. Each edit goes through human review before the catalog changes. Which Google AI capability should produce the images?

choices.text: Document AI, using a processor that extracts fields from the supplier files
Cloud Vision API, using label detection to create new versions of each product photo
Video Intelligence API, using shot detection on frames from supplier clips
Imagen and Gemini image generation on Agent Platform, using prompts and masks to edit and generate images

stem: A broadcaster wants live captions for a livestreamed interview. Text should appear while people are still speaking and correct itself as more audio arrives. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Video Intelligence speech transcription, requested after each segment of the stream is saved to a file
Speech-to-Text batch recognition run once on the full recording after the interview ends
Speech-to-Text streaming recognition over a bidirectional gRPC stream, using interim results
Text-to-Speech on the written transcript, so that the audio is regenerated with captions

stem: A company with about 3,000 employees wants staff to ask questions grounded in content from Google Drive, Jira and SharePoint. Non-developer teams should be able to build multi-step agents themselves, and the company has little engineering capacity for building a platform. Which solution fits best?

choices.text: Gemini Enterprise with data stores connected to the sources, and Workflow Builder for no-code agents
An open model from Model Garden deployed to an endpoint, with custom connectors written for each source
A custom retrieval application built on Agent Platform with a self-managed vector store and its own chat UI
Gemini Notebook Enterprise notebooks created by each team, with all documents uploaded as sources

stem: A compliance team needs to summarize and query a fixed set of dense policy PDFs and slide decks. Answers must be grounded only in those documents, data must stay inside the company's Google Cloud project, and nobody wants to build or operate an application. Which product fits?

choices.text: An open model from Model Garden deployed to an Agent Platform endpoint with a custom retrieval service
Gemini Notebook Enterprise, with the documents added as sources of a notebook
A Gemini Enterprise app connected to every company data source, with the assistant answering from all of it
Vision API OCR on every page, with results stored in BigQuery for later SQL searches

stem: A software team's licensing and security rules require an open-weight model that it can fine-tune on private data and serve on a dedicated endpoint under its own control, instead of calling a hosted model API. The team wants a managed way to discover, customize and deploy it. What should the architect recommend?

choices.text: Call a hosted Gemini model through the API with long prompts, since prompts replace any need for training
Download the model weights from a public repository, copy them to a GKE cluster and build the serving stack by hand
Use Cloud Natural Language API, since its prebuilt model can be retrained on private text
Choose the open model in Model Garden, fine-tune it with a notebook or pipeline, and deploy it to an Agent Platform endpoint

stem: A manufacturer must identify 40 of its own proprietary part types in photos from the factory floor. A pilot with the Cloud Vision API's label detection returns only generic labels such as "metal" and "machine". An ML engineer is available. What should the architect recommend?

choices.text: Keep Vision API label detection and map its generic labels such as machine and metal to the part names with a lookup table
Run Video Intelligence object tracking on stills so that the tracker learns the part types
Switch to the Natural Language API, which has entity analysis for part names
Train or tune a custom image model on labeled part photos in Agent Platform, or use a multimodal model with examples

stem: A company already runs a customer-support virtual agent built with Dialogflow and a custom supply-chain agent built with the Agent Development Kit (ADK) and hosted on Agent Runtime. Leadership wants employees to reach both from the Gemini Enterprise web app without rebuilding them. Which TWO actions fit? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Register the Dialogflow conversational agent with the Gemini Enterprise app as an available agent
Give employees the agents' API endpoints so that each team builds its own chat front end
Recreate both agents from scratch in Workflow Builder, because only agents made there appear in the app
Export the agents' prompts into Model Garden, where Gemini Enterprise lists them as tuned models
Register the ADK agent hosted on Agent Runtime with the Gemini Enterprise app as a custom agent

stem: A research group plans to pre-train a large model on a tightly coupled GPU cluster. The run starts on a fixed date, lasts about six weeks and cannot tolerate waiting for capacity or preemption. The group is willing to commit for a year to lower the cost. Which consumption option fits?

choices.text: On-demand requests made on the start date, with a quota increase approved in advance
A future reservation for capacity blocks of clustered GPUs, with a resource-based commitment attached
Spot VMs for the whole cluster, with checkpoints written every few minutes
Flex-start, because it is discounted and keeps the cluster as long as the run needs

stem: EHR Healthcare's past outages were prolonged because alert emails were ignored and nobody was sure who should lead the response. The operations lead is writing the incident process for the new Google Cloud platform that serves hospitals and insurers. Which approach best follows the operational excellence pillar?

choices.text: Let the engineer who first notices an issue handle it alone from start to finish, keeping the notes in a personal document for a later summary
Remove paging altogether and hold a weekly review of all alerts, so that engineers are not distracted from planned feature work by minor problems
Define incident roles, document escalation paths in a runbook, and track every incident in one central incident management system
Rely on one large group chat that everyone is invited to, where the most senior person on the thread decides on actions as the incident goes on

stem: Cymbal Retail's on-call engineers are paged several times a week for the same condition: a queue-consumer deployment stops pulling messages, and the fix is always the same documented, safe restart. The team wants to remove this toil and shorten recovery without losing sight of the underlying problem. Which design best follows the operational excellence pillar?

choices.text: Extend the wiki page with the restart steps and keep paging a human for every occurrence, so that every recovery stays under direct human control
Restart all consumer deployments every hour on a fixed schedule whatever their state, so that the stalled condition can no longer appear in practice
Silence the alert and let engineers restart the consumers by hand whenever customers complain, because a restart needs no judgement and pages add noise
Route the alert to a Pub/Sub notification channel that triggers an automation running the documented restart, and still log each event for later root cause review

stem: Cymbal Retail runs its Kubernetes workloads with an open source monitoring stack of Prometheus servers and Grafana dashboards, and the team's PromQL alerts and dashboards represent years of work. Operating and scaling the Prometheus servers across clusters takes too much effort, and the team wants one global view of metrics. Which approach should the architect recommend?

choices.text: Adopt Managed Service for Prometheus with managed collection, keeping the existing PromQL queries, Grafana dashboards and alert rules
Rewrite every dashboard and alert as a native Cloud Monitoring chart or condition first, and only then retire the Prometheus servers from service
Keep self-managed Prometheus servers on larger machines, and copy their data into BigQuery nightly to answer questions across clusters
Replace metrics with log-based counters only, because logs already carry the required information and no collectors would have to be operated

stem: A checkout service writes a log line with the text PAYMENT_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT each time a call to the card processor times out. The team cannot change the application code before the next release, yet wants a chart of timeouts per minute and a page when the rate rises. What should the architect recommend?

choices.text: Export all logs to Cloud Storage every hour, have an engineer count the matching lines with a script and email the result to the team
Enable Data Access audit logs on the project, because the audit entries record the timeouts that the application experienced with the processor
Create a counter log-based metric that matches those log entries, chart it in Cloud Monitoring and attach an alerting policy to it
Add custom instrumentation with a metrics client library to the service, deploy it with the next release and build the chart afterwards

stem: Cymbal Retail's checkout runs six replicas on GKE. During node upgrades, drains sometimes evict several checkout Pods at almost the same moment, capacity drops and shoppers see errors until the Pods are rescheduled. Which change best protects availability during upgrades?

choices.text: Raise the CPU limit of each checkout Pod, so that the replicas remaining after a drain can absorb the load of the evicted ones
Define a PodDisruptionBudget for checkout that keeps a minimum number of replicas available, so node drains evict its Pods gradually
Disable node auto-upgrades for the cluster, so that maintenance never evicts any Pods and the team upgrades when it has time
Reduce the checkout deployment to two replicas, so that each node drain has fewer Pods to evict and the process finishes faster

stem: Altostrat Media runs Kubernetes clusters both on premises and in Google Cloud, and central operations wants each cluster to carry the same namespaces, network policies and role bindings. Manual changes with kubectl have caused differences between clusters. Which approach best meets the need?

choices.text: Give every cluster administrator a shared script that applies the configuration, and ask them to run it after each change in the repository
Store the desired configuration in a Git repository and use Config Sync to reconcile each cluster to it, reverting manual differences
Back up each cluster's configuration nightly into Cloud Storage, and compare the files by hand whenever an incident suggests a difference
Design all workloads for one namespace so that no per-cluster policy is needed, and rely on application teams to follow conventions

stem: A web tier runs on a regional managed instance group of 12 VMs behind a load balancer. When the team rolls out a new instance template, the group briefly serves errors because too many VMs are replaced at once and some new VMs receive traffic before the application is ready. Which action best fixes the rollout?

choices.text: Update each VM in place by connecting over SSH and changing the package version, one VM at a time during off-peak hours
Raise the load balancer's idle timeout so that in-flight requests are not interrupted while VMs are being replaced by the update
Use a proactive rolling update with low maxUnavailable and a surge allowance, plus an application-based health check for new VMs
Delete all VMs in the group at once and let autoscaling create new ones from the new template, which is the fastest rollout method available

stem: A product team merges code to the main branch daily, but a large new pricing feature will take six weeks to complete and must be switched on for customers only on a marketing date. The team wants to avoid a long-lived feature branch that is hard to merge. Which practice fits best?

choices.text: Hold all other teams' releases until the pricing feature is complete, so that the release train only ever contains finished features
Keep the work on a separate long-lived branch for six weeks, then merge and deploy everything together on the launch date
Deploy a separate full copy of the application containing the feature, and switch every customer to it on the launch date by changing DNS
Merge the unfinished feature in small increments behind a feature flag, deploy continuously with it off, and switch it on at launch

stem: Altostrat Media runs a highly available metadata service on a GKE Standard node pool. A previous node upgrade changed the node configuration, the workloads misbehaved on the new nodes, and returning to the old nodes took hours. The team accepts a temporary cost increase if it can validate the workloads on new nodes and go back quickly. Which node upgrade strategy fits?

choices.text: Configure the node pool for blue-green upgrades with a soak time, so the original nodes remain available for rollback until the workloads are validated
Keep the default surge upgrade with maxUnavailable set to zero, because it restores the previous nodes automatically whenever the new Pods fail
Disable auto-upgrade and rebuild the node pool from scratch after each release, deleting the old nodes first so that no stale capacity is kept
Upgrade only the control plane and leave the nodes on their older version indefinitely, because nodes may run any older version without limit

stem: Altostrat Media's CI pipeline pushes a new image to Artifact Registry on every commit, and the repository grows without limit. Images that run in production and the most recent releases must never be deleted, but old untagged and test images should go. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Apply a delete rule by age alone to the whole repository, because images older than one month are never needed for a rollback of a release
Configure cleanup policies with keep rules for release-tagged images and the most recent versions plus a delete rule by age, and test them with a dry run
Stop pushing images from CI and rebuild them from source at deploy time in each cluster, so that the registry holds nothing that needs cleaning
Delete images by hand every quarter after asking each team which tags they still use, because only people can know what is deployed in production

stem: A global SaaS company's customers in one region report errors. The company's own dashboards show healthy application servers and no recent deployments. The on-call engineer suspects a Google Cloud incident and wants to confirm it quickly, and be told automatically next time an incident affects the project's services. What should the architect recommend?

choices.text: Use Personalized Service Health to see Google Cloud incidents relevant to the projects, and set up alerts on service health events
Check the public status page of the cloud provider manually each morning, because it covers every project at the same level of detail
Add much more application-level logging to the servers, because Google-side incidents always appear in the application logs as exceptions
Open a support case for every customer complaint, and wait for the support engineer to confirm whether Google had an incident that day

stem: A team runs a Cloud Run service whose logs contain thousands of stack traces a day. Engineers cannot tell which distinct errors are new after each release, how often each occurs, or which are most urgent. What should the architect recommend to support triage?

choices.text: Create an alert on total log volume and page the team whenever the number of log lines in a minute increases noticeably
Add a unique request identifier to every response and ask customers to quote it whenever they report problems to the support team
Use Error Reporting, which groups error events by root cause, shows counts and first and last occurrence, and notifies about new groups
Export logs to Cloud Storage and ask engineers to read the files each morning, sorting the stack traces by hand into categories

stem: EHR Healthcare's past outages were prolonged because email alerts reached engineers with no context. The operations lead is defining a new Cloud Monitoring alerting policy for the hospital portal and wants whoever is paged to know quickly what to check. Which TWO changes help most? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Replace the alerting policy with a weekly report of past incidents, so that responders can study the context at leisure instead of paging
Send every alert in the project to one shared mailbox with a generic subject, so that all responders see exactly the same information
Remove the documentation and keep the notification as short as possible, because responders are expected to know every service by heart
Use documentation variables so that each notification names the policy and condition that fired and lists the labels of the affected resource
Add user-defined documentation to the alerting policy with likely causes, first checks and a link to the runbook, delivered with every notification

stem: A support team investigating slow orders must count, for the last week, how many requests exceeded two seconds per customer tier and per hour, across several million log entries, and then join the result with trace data. The Logs Explorer cannot aggregate this way. What should the architect recommend?

choices.text: Reduce the log retention to one day so that the number of entries to review is small enough for Logs Explorer to handle
Create one log-based counter metric for every combination of customer tier and hour, so that the answer is available on a chart
Download the matching entries from Logs Explorer as files and aggregate them in a spreadsheet each time a new question comes up
Enable analytics on the log bucket and use Observability Analytics to run SQL that groups and aggregates the entries and charts the results

stem: A CTO wants to know whether the engineering organization's recent move to automated pipelines and smaller releases has improved software delivery performance. Which TWO measures are DORA delivery metrics that answer this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Deployment frequency, meaning how often the organization deploys to production
Number of tickets closed by the operations team per week, counted regardless of what caused the tickets
Lines of code written per developer per month, as an indicator of how much productive work is being done
Percentage of servers in the fleet that have the monitoring agent installed on them
Change failure rate, meaning the share of deployments that cause a failure in production that needs remediation

stem: A team deploys through a Cloud Deploy delivery pipeline to staging and then production. After each staging deployment, an engineer clicks through the application by hand and promotes the release if it looks fine. Last month a broken release was promoted because the check was skipped. Which change makes the quality check consistent?

choices.text: Add a longer written checklist for the engineer to follow after every staging deployment, and require a second engineer to initial it before promotion
Configure deployment verification on the staging target with a test container that exits with a failure code on errors, so a failed check fails the rollout
Promote automatically to production as soon as the staging deployment finishes, and rely on production monitoring to notice a broken release
Run the same smoke tests on developer laptops before merging only, because a deployed staging environment cannot be checked by automated tests

stem: A health-software vendor's staging environment holds a stale, tiny data set, so slow queries and edge cases appear only in production. Engineers propose copying the production patient database into staging. The compliance officer objects. Which approach best improves test quality while respecting privacy?

choices.text: Keep the small data set and add a note to the release checklist stating that performance was not tested on realistic data
Fill staging with random text values of the same length as production fields, generated once, as a quick way to make large tables
De-identify the copy with Sensitive Data Protection first, for example masking or tokenizing identifiers, so volume and shape stay realistic
Copy production data unchanged, but restrict staging to a smaller group of engineers who have signed a confidentiality agreement

stem: A team's integration test suite fails randomly about one run in ten, with no code change. Developers have started clicking re-run until the pipeline passes, and a real regression slipped through last week unnoticed because "it is just the flaky test". Which action best restores confidence in the quality gate?

choices.text: Make the pipeline retry every failing test up to five times automatically, and report success if any one attempt passes
Keep the suite as it is but make the pipeline non-blocking, so that releases are never delayed by test failures
Quarantine the unreliable tests from the blocking gate while they are fixed with a tracked owner, and find causes such as shared state or timing
Remove the integration tests, because unit tests alone are faster and never produce intermittent results in the pipeline

stem: A platform team wants to practise failure handling for a stateless service on regional GKE. It plans a game day in production that terminates nodes. Which approach reflects good chaos engineering practice?

choices.text: State the expected steady-state behaviour, start with one node at low traffic, watch alerts, stop on agreed limits, and expand gradually
Terminate all nodes in every zone at the busiest time of the week to see whether anything breaks, with no advance notice to other teams
Run random failures continuously from day one with no monitoring in place, and read the incident tickets next quarter to see what went wrong
Run the experiment only in a laptop environment with no traffic, since failures in a production-like setting are never worth the risk

stem: KnightMotives runs the dealer-order database on Cloud SQL with high availability enabled. The team assumes failover is automatic, but nobody has seen how the ordering application behaves when the primary instance fails over. Which TWO actions give the best evidence? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Read the high availability documentation and record that failover is automatic, so the application is assumed to recover without any interruption
Wait for the next real zonal outage in production, and judge the application's behaviour afterwards from the incident report
Turn off high availability on the instance, because a standalone instance has no failover that the application would ever have to handle
Measure how long connections fail and how quickly the application reconnects, then compare the result with the recovery target set by the business
Manually initiate a failover on a pre-production instance with the same HA configuration while the application runs a realistic load

stem: KnightMotives is rebuilding its unreliable online build-to-order system, which pulls stock and supply data from an older mainframe-based ERP. Dealers' traffic spikes when a new model opens for orders. Before launch, the architect plans load testing. Which plan is most valuable?

choices.text: Skip load testing and rely on autoscaling to absorb any traffic, since managed services never reach a capacity limit of any kind
Replay realistic order mixes against a production-like environment, ramp beyond the launch peak, and watch autoscaling, latency and ERP load
Send a constant light load of identical requests for ten minutes to the web tier only, and declare success if no errors occur
Test only the new application with the ERP dependency replaced by a fast stub, so that the results show the cloud components at their best

stem: A company plans an annual penetration test of its customer portal, run by an outside security firm. Which TWO actions make the test most valuable? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Hide the test from the operations and security monitoring teams, so that no one knows whether the activity is real or authorized
Aim the test at Google's shared infrastructure and at other customers' resources, to see whether they can be reached from the portal
Run the test only against a staging copy with different identities and network paths, because production must never be tested
Include the disaster recovery environment in the scope, because it is a production-equivalent target that attackers could use
Use the test to check that logging, alerts and the incident response process detect and escalate the simulated attacks

stem: KnightMotives' build-to-order front end runs on Cloud Run and writes every dealer order into the mainframe ERP, which handles only a modest steady request rate and slows badly under bursts. When a new model opens for orders, the ERP collapses and checkout fails for everyone. Orders may be processed a few minutes after they are placed. Which change best improves resilience?

choices.text: Put orders into a Cloud Tasks queue with dispatch rate and concurrency limits toward the ERP, so bursts are absorbed and sent at a pace it can handle
Raise the maximum number of Cloud Run instances, so that more order requests reach the ERP in parallel and the burst is finished sooner
Cache the ERP's responses at the load balancer, so that repeated order submissions are answered without calling the ERP again
Keep calling the ERP synchronously from every web request and increase the client timeout, so that slow answers are still accepted as success

stem: A company takes nightly backups of its Cloud SQL databases and has never restored one. After a bad deployment corrupted data, the team wants to be sure that recovery will work next time. Which approach does the reliability pillar recommend?

choices.text: Increase backup frequency to hourly and keep the restore procedure undocumented, since frequent backups remove the need to practise
Regularly restore backups into non-production, check integrity, bring up the full stack and measure the time and data loss against RTO and RPO
Check that the backup job reports success each night, since a success status proves that the data can be restored when needed
Restore a backup into the production database instance to prove that it works, and accept a short interruption while it runs
